ग्रहणोत्पातभं क्रूरविद्धर्क्षं क्रूरसंयुतम् ॥
1.56.m: An inauspicious muhūrta (durmuhūrta); the blemish of the weekday; an asterism sharing the same quarter in the khārjūra diagram; / an asterism afflicted by an eclipse or portent, or pierced by a malefic, or conjoined with a malefic;

1.56.s:
kunavāṃśo mahāpāto vaidhṛtiścaikaviṃśatiḥ /
tithivārarkṣayogānāṃ karaṇasya ca melanam //
1.56.d:
कुनवांशो महापातो वैधृतिश्चैकविंशतिः ।
तिथिवारर्क्षयोगानां करणस्य च मेलनम् ॥
1.56.m: An evil navāṃśa; the great fall (mahāpāta); and Vaidhṛti makes twenty-one. / The combination of tithi, weekday, asterism, yoga,

1.56.s:
pañcāṅgamasya śuddhistu pañcāṅgaśuddhirīritā /
yasminpañcāṅgadoṣo 'sti tasmiṃllagne nirarthakam //
1.56.d:
पञ्चाङ्गमस्य शुद्धिस्तु पञ्चाङ्गशुद्धिरीरिता ।
यस्मिन्पञ्चाङ्गदोषो ऽस्ति तस्मिंल्लग्ने निरर्थकम् ॥
1.56.m: And karaṇa is the five limbs (pañcāṅga); its purity is declared to be pañcāṅga-śuddhi. / The lagna in which there is a defect of the five limbs is useless;

1.56.s:
tyajetpañcaiṣṭikaṃ cāpi viṣasaṃyuktadugdhavat /
lagnalagnāṃśakau svasvapatinā vīkṣitau yutau //
1.56.d:
त्यजेत्पञ्चैष्टिकं चापि विषसंयुक्तदुग्धवत् ।
लग्नलग्नांशकौ स्वस्वपतिना वीक्षितौ युतौ ॥
1.56.m: Even if five desires are fulfilled, one should abandon it like milk mixed with poison. / If the lagna and the navāṃśa of the lagna are not aspected by or conjoined with their respective lords,

1.56.s:
na cedvānyonyapatinā śubhaghamitreṇa vā tathā /
varasya mṛtyuḥ syāttābhyāṃ saptasaptodayāṃśakau //
1.56.d:
न चेद्वान्योन्यपतिना शुभघमित्रेण वा तथा ।
वरस्य मृत्युः स्यात्ताभ्यां सप्तसप्तोदयांशकौ ॥
1.56.m: Or not by each other's lord, or likewise by an auspicious friend, / death of the groom will occur through both of them. If the seventh house and the navāṃśa of the seventh

1.56.s:
evaṃ tau na yutau dṛṣṭau mutyurvadhvāḥ karagrahe /
tyājyāḥ sūryasya saṃkrānteḥ pūrvataḥ paratastathā //
1.56.d:
एवं तौ न युतौ दृष्टौ मुत्युर्वध्वाः करग्रहे ।
त्याज्याः सूर्यस्य संक्रान्तेः पूर्वतः परतस्तथा ॥
1.56.m: Are likewise not conjoined or aspected, death of the bride occurs in marriage. / Before and after the Sun's transit (saṃkrānti),

1.56.s:
vivāhādiṣu kāryeṣu nāḍyaḥ ṣoḍaśaṣoḍaśā / /
ṣaḍvargaḥ śubhadaḥ śreṣṭho vivāhasathāpanādiṣu //
1.56.d:
विवाहादिषु कार्येषु नाड्यः षोडशषोडशा । ।
षड्वर्गः शुभदः श्रेष्ठो विवाहसथापनादिषु ॥
1.56.m: Sixteen nāḍīs in each direction are to be avoided in activities such as marriage. / An auspicious sixfold division (ṣaḍvarga) is excellent in marriage, consecrations, and the like.

1.56.s:
bhṛguṣaṣṭhāhvayo doṣo lagnātṣaṣṭhagate site /
uccage śubhasaṃyukte tallagnaṃ sarvadā tyajet //
1.56.d:
भृगुषष्ठाह्वयो दोषो लग्नात्षष्ठगते सिते ।
उच्चगे शुभसंयुक्ते तल्लग्नं सर्वदा त्यजेत् ॥
1.56.m: The fault named 'Venus in the sixth' occurs when Venus occupies the sixth house from the lagna; / even if exalted or conjoined with a benefic, one should always avoid that lagna.

1.56.s:
kujo 'ṣṭamo mahādoṣo lagnādaṣṭamage kuje /
śubhatrayayutaṃ lagnaṃ na tyajettuṅgago yadi //
1.56.d:
कुजो ऽष्टमो महादोषो लग्नादष्टमगे कुजे ।
शुभत्रययुतं लग्नं न त्यजेत्तुङ्गगो यदि ॥
1.56.m: 'Mars in the eighth' is a great blemish when Mars occupies the eighth house from the lagna; / yet one need not abandon a lagna conjoined with three benefics if Mars is in his exaltation.

1.56.s:
pūrṇānandāṅkhyayostithyoḥ saṃdhirnāḍīdvayaṃ yadā /
gaṇḍāntaṃ mṛtyudaṃ janmayātrodvāhavratādiṣu //
1.56.d:
पूर्णानन्दाङ्ख्ययोस्तिथ्योः संधिर्नाडीद्वयं यदा ।
गण्डान्तं मृत्युदं जन्मयात्रोद्वाहव्रतादिषु ॥
1.56.m: When the junction of the tithis called Pūrṇā and Nandā lasts two nāḍīs, / it is gaṇḍānta, which causes death in birth, journeys, marriages, vows, and the like.

1.56.s:
kulīrasiṃhayoḥ kīṭacāpayorminameṣayoḥ /
gaṇḍātaṃmantarālaṃ syāddhaṭikārddhaṃ mṛtipradam //
1.56.d:
कुलीरसिंहयोः कीटचापयोर्मिनमेषयोः ।
गण्डातंमन्तरालं स्याद्धटिकार्द्धं मृतिप्रदम् ॥
1.56.m: Between Cancer and Leo, Scorpio and Sagittarius, and Pisces and Aries, / the interval is gaṇḍānta; half a ghaṭikā there bestows death.

1.56.s:
sārpaindrapauṣṇobheṣvantyaṣoḍaśeśā bhasaṃdhayaḥ /
tadagnimeṣvādyapādā bhānāṃ gaṇḍātasaṃjñakāḥ //
1.56.d:
सार्पैन्द्रपौष्णोभेष्वन्त्यषोडशेशा भसंधयः ।
तदग्निमेष्वाद्यपादा भानां गण्डातसंज्ञकाः ॥
1.56.m: At the junctions of the asterisms Āśleṣā, Jyeṣṭhā, and Revatī—the last sixteen nāḍīs are the nakṣatra-junctions; / the first quarters of Aśvinī, Maghā, and Mūla are also termed gaṇḍānta.

1.56.s:
ugraṃ ca saṃdhitritayaṃ gaṇḍātaṃ trividhaṃ mahat /
lagnābhimukhayoḥ pāpagrahayorṛjuvakrayoḥ //
1.56.d:
उग्रं च संधित्रितयं गण्डातं त्रिविधं महत् ।
लग्नाभिमुखयोः पापग्रहयोरृजुवक्रयोः ॥
1.56.m: Fierce is this triad of junctions, the great threefold gaṇḍānta. / When two malefic planets face the lagna, one in direct and the other in retrograde motion,

1.56.s:
sā kartarīti vijñeyā daṃpatyorgalakartarī /
kartarīyogaduṣṭaṃ yallagnaṃ tatparivarjayet //
1.56.d:
सा कर्तरीति विज्ञेया दंपत्योर्गलकर्तरी ।
कर्तरीयोगदुष्टं यल्लग्नं तत्परिवर्जयेत् ॥
1.56.m: That is to be known as the scissors-formation (kartarī), a throat-cutter for the couple; / a lagna corrupted by the kartarī yoga one must utterly avoid,

1.56.s:
api saumyagrahairyukta guṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ samanvitam /
ṣaḍaṣṭariṣphage candre lagnadoṣaḥ svasaṃjñakaḥ //
1.56.d:
अपि सौम्यग्रहैर्युक्त गुणैः सर्वैः समन्वितम् ।
षडष्टरिष्फगे चन्द्रे लग्नदोषः स्वसंज्ञकः ॥
1.56.m: Even if it is conjoined with benefic planets and endowed with all good qualities. / When the Moon is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, that constitutes the lagna-fault named after them.

1.56.s:
tallagnaṃ varjayedyatrājjīvaśukrasamanvitam /
uccage nīcage vāpi mitrabhe śatrurāśige //
1.56.d:
तल्लग्नं वर्जयेद्यत्राज्जीवशुक्रसमन्वितम् ।
उच्चगे नीचगे वापि मित्रभे शत्रुराशिगे ॥
1.56.m: One should diligently avoid that lagna even if conjoined with Jupiter and Venus, / whether [the Moon is] in exaltation or debilitation, in a friendly sign or in an enemy's sign;

1.56.s:
api sarvaguṇopetaṃ daṃpatyornidhanapradam /
śaśāṅke grahasaṃyukte doṣaḥ saṃgrahasaṃjñakaḥ //
1.56.d:
अपि सर्वगुणोपेतं दंपत्योर्निधनप्रदम् ।
शशाङ्के ग्रहसंयुक्ते दोषः संग्रहसंज्ञकः ॥
1.56.m: Even if endowed with all virtues, it brings death to the couple. / When the Moon is conjoined with a planet, it is the blemish called saṃgraha.

1.56.s:
tasminsaṃgrahadoṣe tu vivāhaṃ naiva kārayet /
sūryeṇa saṃyute candre dāridyaṃ bhavati sphuṭam //
1.56.d:
तस्मिन्संग्रहदोषे तु विवाहं नैव कारयेत् ।
सूर्येण संयुते चन्द्रे दारिद्यं भवति स्फुटम् ॥
1.56.m: During that saṃgraha fault, one should never perform a marriage. / When the Moon is conjoined with the Sun, poverty clearly results;

1.56.s:
kujena maraṇaṃ vyādhiḥ saumyena tvanapatyatā /
daurbhāgyaṃ guruṇā yukte sāpatyaṃ bhārgaveṇa tu //
1.56.d:
कुजेन मरणं व्याधिः सौम्येन त्वनपत्यता ।
दौर्भाग्यं गुरुणा युक्ते सापत्यं भार्गवेण तु ॥
1.56.m: With Mars, death; with Mercury, disease and childlessness; / with Jupiter, misfortune; with Venus, children;

1.56.s:
pravrajyā sūryaputreṇa rāhuṇā mūlasaṃkṣayaḥ /
ketunā saṃyute candre nityaṃ kaṣṭaṃ daridratā //
1.56.d:
प्रव्रज्या सूर्यपुत्रेण राहुणा मूलसंक्षयः ।
केतुना संयुते चन्द्रे नित्यं कष्टं दरिद्रता ॥
1.56.m: With Saturn, renunciation; with Rāhu, total destruction of the family; / when the Moon is conjoined with Ketu, constant distress and indigence.

1.56.s:
pāpagrahayute candre daṃpatyormaraṇaṃ bhavet /
śubhagrahayute candre svoccasthe mitrarāśige //
1.56.d:
पापग्रहयुते चन्द्रे दंपत्योर्मरणं भवेत् ।
शुभग्रहयुते चन्द्रे स्वोच्चस्थे मित्रराशिगे ॥
1.56.m: When the Moon is conjoined with a malefic planet, death of the couple occurs; / when the Moon is conjoined with a benefic planet, exalted, or in a friend's sign,

1.56.s:
doṣāyanaṃ bhavellagnaṃ daṃpatyoḥ śreyase sadā /
svoccago vā svarkṣago vā mitra kṣetragatopi vā //
1.56.d:
दोषायनं भवेल्लग्नं दंपत्योः श्रेयसे सदा ।
स्वोच्चगो वा स्वर्क्षगो वा मित्र क्षेत्रगतोपि वा ॥
1.56.m: The lagna becomes an abode of good qualities, always for the welfare of the couple; / but if conjoined with a malefic planet, even if exalted, in its own asterism, or in a friendly sign,

1.56.s:
pāpagnahayutaścandraḥ karoti maraṇaṃ tayoḥ /
daṃpatyoraṣṭamaṃ lagnamaṣṭamo rāśireva ca //
1.56.d:
पापग्नहयुतश्चन्द्रः करोति मरणं तयोः ।
दंपत्योरष्टमं लग्नमष्टमो राशिरेव च ॥
1.56.m: The Moon brings about their death. / If the eighth lagna or eighth sign of the couple

1.56.s:
yadi lagnagataḥ sopi daṃpatyormaraṇapradaḥ /
sa rāśiḥ śubhasaṃyukto lagnaṃ vā śubhasaṃyutam //
1.56.d:
यदि लग्नगतः सोपि दंपत्योर्मरणप्रदः ।
स राशिः शुभसंयुक्तो लग्नं वा शुभसंयुतम् ॥
1.56.m: Itself becomes the rising lagna, it also causes the death of the couple; / even if that sign is conjoined with a benefic, or the lagna is conjoined with a benefic,

1.56.s:
lagnaṃ vivarjayedyatnāttadaṃśāṃśatadīśvarām /
daṃpatyordvādaśaṃ lagnaṃ rāśirvā yadi lagnagaḥ //
1.56.d:
लग्नं विवर्जयेद्यत्नात्तदंशांशतदीश्वराम् ।
दंपत्योर्द्वादशं लग्नं राशिर्वा यदि लग्नगः ॥
1.56.m: One must diligently avoid the lagna, its sub-division (aṃśa), and their lords. / If the twelfth lagna or twelfth sign of the couple becomes the rising lagna,

1.56.s:
arthahānistayorasmāttadaṃśasvāminaṃ tyajet /
janmarāśyudayaścaiva janmalagnodayaḥ śubhaḥ //
1.56.d:
अर्थहानिस्तयोरस्मात्तदंशस्वामिनं त्यजेत् ।
जन्मराश्युदयश्चैव जन्मलग्नोदयः शुभः ॥
1.56.m: Loss of wealth occurs for both; therefore, one should avoid the lord of that aṃśa. / The rising of the birth-sign and the rising of the birth-lagna are auspicious;

1.56.s:
tayorupacayasthānaṃ lagnetyantaśubhapradam /
khamārgaṇā vedapakṣāḥ kharāmā vedamārgaṇāḥ //
1.56.d:
तयोरुपचयस्थानं लग्नेत्यन्तशुभप्रदम् ।
खमार्गणा वेदपक्षाः खरामा वेदमार्गणाः ॥
1.56.m: The upacaya houses of those two, as lagna, bestow supreme good fortune. / [The viṣanāḍīs are:] fifty (khamārgaṇa, 50), twenty-four (vedapakṣa, 24), thirty (kharāma, 30), fifty-four (vedamārgaṇa, 54),

1.56.s:
vahnicandrā rūpadasrāḥ kharāmā vyomabāhavaḥ /
dvirāmāḥ svāgnaṃyaḥ śūnyadasrāḥ kuñjarabhūmayaḥ //
1.56.d:
वह्निचन्द्रा रूपदस्राः खरामा व्योमबाहवः ।
द्विरामाः स्वाग्नंयः शून्यदस्राः कुञ्जरभूमयः ॥
1.56.m: Thirteen (vahnicandra, 13), twenty-one (rūpadasra, 21), thirty (kharāma, 30), twenty (vyomabāhu, 20), / thirty-two (dvirāma, 32), thirty-three (svāgni, 33), twenty (śūnyadasra, 20), eighteen (kuñjarabhūmi, 18),

1.56.s:
rūpapakṣā vyomadasrā vedacandrāścaturddaśa /
śūnyacandrā vedacandrā ṣaḍṛkṣā vedabāhavaḥ //
1.56.d:
रूपपक्षा व्योमदस्रा वेदचन्द्राश्चतुर्द्दश ।
शून्यचन्द्रा वेदचन्द्रा षडृक्षा वेदबाहवः ॥
1.56.m: Twenty-one (rūpapakṣa, 21), twenty (vyomadasra, 20), fourteen (vedacandra, 14), fourteen (caturdaśa, 14), / ten (śūnyacandra, 10), fourteen (vedacandra, 14), twenty-six (ṣaḍṛkṣa, 26), twenty-four (vedabāhu, 24),

1.56.s:
śūnyadasrāḥ śūnyacandrāḥ pūrṇacandrā gatendravaḥ /
tarkacandrā vedapakṣāḥ kharāmāścāśvibhātkramāt //
1.56.d:
शून्यदस्राः शून्यचन्द्राः पूर्णचन्द्रा गतेन्द्रवः ।
तर्कचन्द्रा वेदपक्षाः खरामाश्चाश्विभात्क्रमात् ॥
1.56.m: Twenty (śūnyadasra, 20), ten (śūnyacandra, 10), ten (pūrṇacandra, 10), zero (gatendrava, 0), / sixteen (tarkacandra, 16), twenty-four (vedapakṣa, 24), and thirty (kharāma, 30), in order from the asterism Aśvinī.

1.56.s:
ābhyāḥ parāstu ghaṭikāścatasro viṣasaṃjñitāḥ /
vivāhādiṣu kāryeṣu viṣanāḍīṃ vivarjayet //
1.56.d:
आभ्याः परास्तु घटिकाश्चतस्रो विषसंज्ञिताः ।
विवाहादिषु कार्येषु विषनाडीं विवर्जयेत् ॥
1.56.m: The four ghaṭikās following these are designated as poison [ghaṭikās]; / in marriage and other rituals, one should avoid the poisonous nāḍī.

1.56.s:
bhāskarādiṣu vāreṣu ye muhūrtāśca ninditāḥ /
vivāhādiṣu te varjyā apilakṣaguṇairyutāḥ //
1.56.d:
भास्करादिषु वारेषु ये मुहूर्ताश्च निन्दिताः ।
विवाहादिषु ते वर्ज्या अपिलक्षगुणैर्युताः ॥
1.56.m: The muhūrtas censured on the weekdays beginning with Sunday / should be avoided in marriage and other rites, even if endowed with a hundred thousand good qualities.

1.56.s:
nihitāvāradoṣā ye sūryavārādiṣu kramāt /
api sarvaguṇopetāste varjyāḥ sarvamaṅgale //
1.56.d:
निहितावारदोषा ये सूर्यवारादिषु क्रमात् ।
अपि सर्वगुणोपेतास्ते वर्ज्याः सर्वमङ्गले ॥
1.56.m: The flaws assigned to the weekdays in succession, beginning with Sunday, / must be avoided in every auspicious rite, even if endowed with all virtues.

1.56.s:
ekārgalāṅghritulyaṃ yattallagnaṃ ca vivarjayet /
apiśukrejyasaṃyuktaṃ viṣasaṃyuktadugdhavat //
1.56.d:
एकार्गलाङ्घ्रितुल्यं यत्तल्लग्नं च विवर्जयेत् ।
अपिशुक्रेज्यसंयुक्तं विषसंयुक्तदुग्धवत् ॥
1.56.m: One must avoid an ascendant that corresponds to a quarter of Ekārgala, / even if conjoined with Venus and Jupiter, like milk mixed with poison.

1.56.s:
grahaṇotpātabhaṃ tyājyaṃ maṅgaleṣu ṛtutrayam /
yāvacca śaśinā bhuktvā muktabhaṃ dagdhakāṣṭavat //
1.56.d:
ग्रहणोत्पातभं त्याज्यं मङ्गलेषु ऋतुत्रयम् ।
यावच्च शशिना भुक्त्वा मुक्तभं दग्धकाष्टवत् ॥
1.56.m: The constellation of an eclipse or portent is to be avoided in auspicious rites for three seasons, / and an asterism traversed and abandoned by the Moon [is avoided] like burnt wood.

1.56.s:
maṅgaleṣu tyajetśeṭairviddhaṃ ca krūrasaṃyutam /
akhilarkṣaṃ pañcagavyaṃ surābinduyutaṃ tathā //
1.56.d:
मङ्गलेषु त्यजेत्शेटैर्विद्धं च क्रूरसंयुतम् ।
अखिलर्क्षं पञ्चगव्यं सुराबिन्दुयुतं तथा ॥
1.56.m: In auspicious rites, one should avoid an entire asterism pierced by planets or conjoined with a malefic, / like the five products of the cow mixed with a drop of liquor.

1.56.s:
pāda eva śubhairviddhamaśubhaṃ naiva kṛtstrabham /
krūraviddhaṃ yutaṃ dhiṣṇyaṃ nikhilaṃ naiva maṅgalam //
1.56.d:
पाद एव शुभैर्विद्धमशुभं नैव कृत्स्त्रभम् ।
क्रूरविद्धं युतं धिष्ण्यं निखिलं नैव मङ्गलम् ॥
1.56.m: When pierced by benefics, only that quarter is inauspicious, not the whole asterism; / an asterism pierced or joined by a malefics is entirely devoid of auspiciousness.

1.56.s:
tulāmithunakanyāṃśā dhanurantyārddhasaṃyutāḥ /
ete navāṃśāḥ śubhadā vṛṣabhasyāṃśakāḥ khalu //
1.56.d:
तुलामिथुनकन्यांशा धनुरन्त्यार्द्धसंयुताः ।
एते नवांशाः शुभदा वृषभस्यांशकाः खलु ॥
1.56.m: The navāṃśas of Libra, Gemini, and Virgo, joined with the latter half of Sagittarius, / and indeed the navāṃśas of Taurus—these navāṃśas bestow auspiciousness.

1.56.s:
antyāṃśāstepi śubhadā yadi vargottamāhvayāḥ /
anye navāṃśā na grāhyā yataste kunavāṃśakāḥ //
1.56.d:
अन्त्यांशास्तेपि शुभदा यदि वर्गोत्तमाह्वयाः ।
अन्ये नवांशा न ग्राह्या यतस्ते कुनवांशकाः ॥
1.56.m: The final navāṃśas are also auspicious if they are called vargottama; / other navāṃśas are not to be accepted, because they are bad navāṃśas.

1.56.s:
kunavāṃśakalagnaṃ yattyājyaṃ sarvaguṇānvitam /
yasmindine mahāpātastaddinaṃ varjayecchubhe //
1.56.d:
कुनवांशकलग्नं यत्त्याज्यं सर्वगुणान्वितम् ।
यस्मिन्दिने महापातस्तद्दिनं वर्जयेच्छुभे ॥
1.56.m: An ascendant in a bad navāṃśa is to be discarded, even if endowed with all virtues. / The day on which a mahāpāta occurs should be avoided in auspicious rites;

1.56.s:
api sarvaguṇopetaṃ dampatyormṛtyudaṃ yataḥ /
anuktāḥ svalpadoṣāḥ syurvidyunnīhāravṛṣṭayaḥ //
1.56.d:
अपि सर्वगुणोपेतं दम्पत्योर्मृत्युदं यतः ।
अनुक्ताः स्वल्पदोषाः स्युर्विद्युन्नीहारवृष्टयः ॥
1.56.m: even if endowed with all virtues, it brings death to the couple. / Minor flaws, which are not mentioned [as destructive], are lightning, mist, rain,

1.56.s:
pratyarkapariveṣendracāpāṃbudharagarjanāḥ /
lattopagrahapātākhyā māsadagdhāhvayā tithiḥ //
1.56.d:
प्रत्यर्कपरिवेषेन्द्रचापांबुधरगर्जनाः ।
लत्तोपग्रहपाताख्या मासदग्धाह्वया तिथिः ॥
1.56.m: mock suns, halos, rainbows, thunder, / lattā, upagraha, pātā, and the lunar day called māsadagdha;

1.56.s:
dagdhalagnāndhabadhirapaṅgusaṃjñāśca rāśayaḥ /
evamādyāstatasteṣāṃ vyavasthā kriyate 'dhunā //
1.56.d:
दग्धलग्नान्धबधिरपङ्गुसंज्ञाश्च राशयः ।
एवमाद्यास्ततस्तेषां व्यवस्था क्रियते ऽधुना ॥
1.56.m: and the zodiacal signs designated as burnt ascendants, blind, deaf, and lame. / Their status is now set forth regarding these and similar matters:

1.56.s:
akālajā bhavantyete vidyunnīhāravṛṣṭayaḥ /
doṣāya maṅgale nūnamadoṣāyaiva kālataḥ //
1.56.d:
अकालजा भवन्त्येते विद्युन्नीहारवृष्टयः ।
दोषाय मङ्गले नूनमदोषायैव कालतः ॥
1.56.m: When these—lightning, mist, and rain—occur out of season, / they certainly cause defect in an auspicious rite, but in their proper season they cause no defect at all.

1.56.s:
bṛhaspatiḥ kendragataḥ śukro vā yadi vā budhaḥ /
eko 'pi doṣanicayaṃ haratyeva na saṃśayaḥ //
1.56.d:
बृहस्पतिः केन्द्रगतः शुक्रो वा यदि वा बुधः ।
एको ऽपि दोषनिचयं हरत्येव न संशयः ॥
1.56.m: If Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury / is placed in an angle, even one [of them] destroys the multitude of faults; of this there is no doubt.

1.56.s:
tiryakpañcorddhūgāḥ pañca rekhā dve dve ca koṇayoḥ /
dvitīye śaṃbhukoṇe 'gnidhiṣṇyaṃ cakre pravinyaset //
1.56.d:
तिर्यक्पञ्चोर्द्धूगाः पञ्च रेखा द्वे द्वे च कोणयोः ।
द्वितीये शंभुकोणे ऽग्निधिष्ण्यं चक्रे प्रविन्यसेत् ॥
1.56.m: Draw five horizontal lines, five vertical lines, and two in each corner; / in this diagram, one should place the asterism of Agni [Kṛttikā] in the second corner, the north-east.

1.56.s:
bhānyatra sābhijityekarekhākheṭena viddhabham /
purataḥ pṛṣṭator'kādyā dinarkṣaṃ lattayanti yat //
1.56.d:
भान्यत्र साभिजित्येकरेखाखेटेन विद्धभम् ।
पुरतः पृष्टतोर्ऽकाद्या दिनर्क्षं लत्तयन्ति यत् ॥
1.56.m: The asterisms, including Abhijit, situated on the same line are asterisms pierced by a planet. / The planets, beginning with the Sun, which pierce the asterism of the day from the front or the back,

1.56.s:
arkākṛtiguṇādynaṅgabāṇāṣṭanavasaṃkhyabham /
sūryabhātsārppapitryāntyatvāṣṭramitroḍuviṣṇubham //
1.56.d:
अर्काकृतिगुणाद्य्नङ्गबाणाष्टनवसंख्यभम् ।
सूर्यभात्सार्प्पपित्र्यान्त्यत्वाष्ट्रमित्रोडुविष्णुभम् ॥
1.56.m: strike the asterism numbering twelve, three, nine, six, five, eight, or nine / from the Sun's asterism, [or] the asterisms of the serpents [Āśleṣā], the ancestors [Maghā], the last [Revatī], Tvaṣṭṛ [Citrā], Mitra [Anurādhā], or Viṣṇu [Śravaṇa].

1.56.s:
saṃkhyāyā dinabhetāvadaśvibhātpātaduṣṭabham /
saurāṣṭre sālvadeśe tu lattitaṃ bhaṃ vivarjayet //
1.56.d:
संख्याया दिनभेतावदश्विभात्पातदुष्टभम् ।
सौराष्ट्रे साल्वदेशे तु लत्तितं भं विवर्जयेत् ॥
1.56.m: By counting to the daily asterism from Aśvinī, the asterism corrupted by pāta is found. / In Saurāṣṭra and the Sālva country, one must avoid an asterism struck by lattā;

1.56.s:
kaliṅgavaṅgadeśeṣu pātitaṃ na śubhapradam /
bāhlike kurudeśe cānyasmindeśe na dūṣaṇam //
1.56.d:
कलिङ्गवङ्गदेशेषु पातितं न शुभप्रदम् ।
बाह्लिके कुरुदेशे चान्यस्मिन्देशे न दूषणम् ॥
1.56.m: [an asterism] afflicted by pāta does not bestow auspiciousness in the lands of Kaliṅga and Vaṅga; / in Bāhlika and the Kuru country and elsewhere it is not a defect.

1.56.s:
tithayo māsadagdhāśca dagdhalagnāni yānyapi /
madhyadeśe vivarjyāni na dṛṣṭānītareṣu ca //
1.56.d:
तिथयो मासदग्धाश्च दग्धलग्नानि यान्यपि ।
मध्यदेशे विवर्ज्यानि न दृष्टानीतरेषु च ॥
1.56.m: The lunar days that are māsadagdha and the ascendants that are burnt / are to be avoided in the Madhyadeśa; they are not considered [flaws] in other regions.

1.56.s:
ṣaṅgvaṃ dhakāṇalagnāni māsaśūnyāśca rāśayaḥ /
gauḍamālavayostyājyā anyadeśe na garhitāḥ //
1.56.d:
षङ्ग्वं धकाणलग्नानि मासशून्याश्च राशयः ।
गौडमालवयोस्त्याज्या अन्यदेशे न गर्हिताः ॥
1.56.m: Ascendants that are lame, blind, and one-eyed, and signs that are void in a month, / are to be rejected in Gauḍa and Mālava; in other countries they are not censured.

1.56.s:
doṣaduṣṭaṃ sadā kālaṃ sannimārṣṭuṃ na śakyate /
api dhāturato grāhyaṃ doṣālpatvaṃ guṇādhikam //
1.56.d:
दोषदुष्टं सदा कालं सन्निमार्ष्टुं न शक्यते ।
अपि धातुरतो ग्राह्यं दोषाल्पत्वं गुणाधिकम् ॥
1.56.m: Time corrupted by flaws can never be completely cleansed, / even by the Creator; therefore, a lesser degree of flaw and an abundance of virtues should be accepted.

1.56.s:
evaṃ sulagne daṃpatyoḥ kārayetsamyagīkṣaṇam /
hastocchritāṃ caturhastaiścaturasrāṃ samantataḥ //
1.56.d:
एवं सुलग्ने दंपत्योः कारयेत्सम्यगीक्षणम् ।
हस्तोच्छ्रितां चतुर्हस्तैश्चतुरस्रां समन्ततः ॥
1.56.m: Thus, at an auspicious ascendant, one should perform the mutual gazing of the bride and groom / [upon an altar] one cubit high, four cubits square on every side,

1.56.s:
staṃbhaścaturbhiḥ suślakṣṇairvāmabhāge tu sannatām /
samaṇḍapāṃ caturdikṣu sopānairatiśobhitām //
1.56.d:
स्तंभश्चतुर्भिः सुश्लक्ष्णैर्वामभागे तु सन्नताम् ।
समण्डपां चतुर्दिक्षु सोपानैरतिशोभिताम् ॥
1.56.m: with four very smooth pillars, sloping towards the left, / furnished with a pavilion, and beautifully adorned with steps on all four sides;

1.56.s:
prāgudakpravaṇāṃ raṃbhāstaṃbhairhaṃsaśukādibhiḥ /
vicitritāṃ citrakuṃbhairvividhaistoraṇāṅkuraiḥ //
1.56.d:
प्रागुदक्प्रवणां रंभास्तंभैर्हंसशुकादिभिः ।
विचित्रितां चित्रकुंभैर्विविधैस्तोरणाङ्कुरैः ॥
1.56.m: sloping towards the north-east, decorated with plantain pillars, swans, parrots, and the like, / with ornamental jars, and various arches and fresh sprouts;

1.56.s:
śṛṅgārapuṣpanicayairvarṇakaiḥ samalaṅkṛtām /
viprāśīrvacanaiḥ puṇyasrībhirdivyairmanoramām //
1.56.d:
शृङ्गारपुष्पनिचयैर्वर्णकैः समलङ्कृताम् ।
विप्राशीर्वचनैः पुण्यस्रीभिर्दिव्यैर्मनोरमाम् ॥
1.56.m: adorned with arrays of auspicious flowers and pigments, / made delightful by the blessings of brāhmaṇas and by holy, celestial women;

1.56.s:
vāditranṛtyagītādyairhṛdayānandinīṃ śubhām /
evaṃ vidhāṃ samārohenmithunaṃ svāgnivedikām //
1.56.d:
वादित्रनृत्यगीताद्यैर्हृदयानन्दिनीं शुभाम् ।
एवं विधां समारोहेन्मिथुनं स्वाग्निवेदिकाम् ॥
1.56.m: gladdening the heart with musical instruments, dancing, songs, and the like, auspicious— / the couple should ascend an altar of fire of such description.

1.56.s:
aṣṭadhā rāśikūṭaṃ ca svādūḍugaṇarāśayaḥ /
rāśīśayonirvarṇākhyaṛtavaḥ putrapautradāḥ //
1.56.d:
अष्टधा राशिकूटं च स्वादूडुगणराशयः ।
राशीशयोनिर्वर्णाख्यऋतवः पुत्रपौत्रदाः ॥
1.56.m: The eightfold agreement of the signs consists of the asterism, the category, the signs, / the lord of the sign, the animal class, the caste, and the seasons, which grant sons and grandsons.

1.56.s:
ekarāśau pṛthagdiṣṇye daṃpatyoḥ pāṇipījanam /
uttamaṃ madhyamaṃ bhinnaṃ rāśyaikatvaṃ yayostayoḥ //
1.56.d:
एकराशौ पृथग्दिष्ण्ये दंपत्योः पाणिपीजनम् ।
उत्तमं मध्यमं भिन्नं राश्यैकत्वं ययोस्तयोः ॥
1.56.m: Marriage of the couple within the same sign but in different asterisms / is best; it is mediocre when the asterism is different and the sign is the same for both.

1.56.s:
ekarkṣe tvekarāśau hi vivāhaḥ prāṇahānidaḥ /
strīdhiṣṇyādādyanavake strīdūramatininditam //
1.56.d:
एकर्क्षे त्वेकराशौ हि विवाहः प्राणहानिदः ।
स्त्रीधिष्ण्यादाद्यनवके स्त्रीदूरमतिनिन्दितम् ॥
1.56.m: Marriage in the same asterism and in the same sign causes loss of life. / If the bridegroom's asterism is in the first ennead from the bride's asterism, it is extremely censured as 'distant from the woman';

1.56.s:
dvitīye madhyamaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ tṛtīye navake nṛbham /
tisraḥ pūrvottarā dhātṛyāmyamāheśatārakāḥ //
1.56.d:
द्वितीये मध्यमं श्रेष्ठं तृतीये नवके नृभम् ।
तिस्रः पूर्वोत्तरा धातृयाम्यमाहेशतारकाः ॥
1.56.m: in the second [ennead] it is mediocre, and in the third ennead the groom's asterism is best. / The three constellations containing Pūrvā and Uttarā, Rohiṇī, Bharaṇī, and Ārdrā—

1.56.s:
iti martyagaṇe jñeyaḥ syādamartyagaṇaḥ paraḥ /
haryādityārkavāyvantyamitrāśvījyendutārakāḥ //
1.56.d:
इति मर्त्यगणे ज्ञेयः स्यादमर्त्यगणः परः ।
हर्यादित्यार्कवाय्वन्त्यमित्राश्वीज्येन्दुतारकाः ॥
1.56.m: these are to be known as the human class; the divine class is different: / Puṣya, Punarvasu, Hastā, Svātī, Revatī, Anurādhā, Aśvinī, Tiṣya [or Puṣya], and Mṛgaśiras.

1.56.s:
rakṣogaṇaḥ pitṛtvāṣṭradvidaivāgnīndratārakāḥ /
vasuvārīśamūlāhitārakābhiryutāstataḥ //
1.56.d:
रक्षोगणः पितृत्वाष्ट्रद्विदैवाग्नीन्द्रतारकाः ।
वसुवारीशमूलाहितारकाभिर्युतास्ततः ॥
1.56.m: The demon class consists of the stars of the ancestors [Maghā], Tvaṣṭṛ [Citrā], the two deities [Viśākhā], fire and Indra [Kṛttikā, Jyeṣṭhā], / together with the stars of the Vasus [Dhaniṣṭhā], the lord of the waters [Śatabhiṣaj], Mūla, and the serpent [Āśleṣā].

1.56.s:
daṃpatyorjanmabhe caikagaṇe prītiranekadhā /
madhyamā devamartyānāṃ rākṣasānāṃ tayormṛtiḥ //
1.56.d:
दंपत्योर्जन्मभे चैकगणे प्रीतिरनेकधा ।
मध्यमा देवमर्त्यानां राक्षसानां तयोर्मृतिः ॥
1.56.m: When the birth-asterisms of the bride and groom belong to the same class, love is manifold; / between divine and human it is middling; [a combination] with demons brings death to both.

1.56.s:
mṛtyuḥ ṣaṣṭāṣṭake pañcanavame tvanapatyatā /
naiḥsvya dvirdvādaśe 'nyeṣu daṃpatyoḥ prītiruttamā //
1.56.d:
मृत्युः षष्टाष्टके पञ्चनवमे त्वनपत्यता ।
नैःस्व्य द्विर्द्वादशे ऽन्येषु दंपत्योः प्रीतिरुत्तमा ॥
1.56.m: Death occurs in a sixth-eighth [sign relationship]; childlessness in a fifth-ninth; / poverty in a second-twelfth; in other [relationships] there is excellent affection between husband and wife.

1.56.s:
ekādhipe mitrabhāve śubhadaṃ pāṇipīḍanam /
dvirdādaśe trikoṇe ca na kadācitṣaḍaṣṭake //
1.56.d:
एकाधिपे मित्रभावे शुभदं पाणिपीडनम् ।
द्विर्दादशे त्रिकोणे च न कदाचित्षडष्टके ॥
1.56.m: When there is the same planetary lord or friendship [between the lords], marriage bestows auspiciousness / in a second-twelfth or a trine [relationship], but never in a sixth-eighth.

1.56.s:
aśvebhameṣasarpāhihyotumeṣotumūṣakāḥ /
ākhugomahiṣavyāghrakālīvyāghramṛgadvayam //
1.56.d:
अश्वेभमेषसर्पाहिह्योतुमेषोतुमूषकाः ।
आखुगोमहिषव्याघ्रकालीव्याघ्रमृगद्वयम् ॥
1.56.m: Horse, elephant, ram, serpent, serpent, dog, cat, ram, cat, rat, / rat, cow, buffalo, tiger, hare, tiger, deer, deer,

1.56.s:
śvānaḥ kaparirbabhruyuge kapisiṃhaturaṅgamāḥ /
siṃhagodantino bhānāṃ yonayaḥ syuryathāśvibhāt //
1.56.d:
श्वानः कपरिर्बभ्रुयुगे कपिसिंहतुरङ्गमाः ।
सिंहगोदन्तिनो भानां योनयः स्युर्यथाश्विभात् ॥
1.56.m: dog, monkey, mongoose pair, monkey, lion, horse, / lion, cow, and elephant are the animal classes of the asterisms in order from Aśvinī.

1.56.s:
śvaiṇaṃ babhraragaṃ meṣavānarau siṃhavāraṇam /
govyāghramākhumārjāraṃ mahiṣāścaṃ ca śātravam //
1.56.d:
श्वैणं बभ्ररगं मेषवानरौ सिंहवारणम् ।
गोव्याघ्रमाखुमार्जारं महिषाश्चं च शात्रवम् ॥
1.56.m: The dog and deer, mongoose and snake, ram and monkey, lion and elephant, / cow and tiger, rat and cat, buffalo and horse are mutual enemies.

1.56.s:
jhaṣālikarkaṭā viprāsta dūrdhvāḥ kṣatriyādayaḥ /
puṃvarṇarāśeḥ strīrāśau satihīne yathāśubham //
1.56.d:
झषालिकर्कटा विप्रास्त दूर्ध्वाः क्षत्रियादयः ।
पुंवर्णराशेः स्त्रीराशौ सतिहीने यथाशुभम् ॥
1.56.m: Pisces, Scorpio, and Cancer are brāhmaṇas; beyond them are the kṣatriyas and the rest. / If the woman's sign is of a lower caste than the man's sign, it is auspicious.

1.56.s:
catustrivdyaṅghribhotthāyāḥ kanyāyāścāśvibhātkramāt /
vahnibhādindubhānnāḍītricatuḥpañcaparvasu //
1.56.d:
चतुस्त्रिव्द्यङ्घ्रिभोत्थायाः कन्यायाश्चाश्विभात्क्रमात् ।
वह्निभादिन्दुभान्नाडीत्रिचतुःपञ्चपर्वसु ॥
1.56.m: For a maiden born in asterisms having four, three, two, or one quarter, in order from Aśvinī, / counting from the asterisms of Agni [Kṛttikā] and the Moon [Rohiṇī], across the three, four, and five nodes,

1.56.s:
gaṇayetsaṃkhyayā caikanāḍyāṃ mṛtyurna pārśvayoḥ /
prājāpatyabrāhmadaivā vivāhāścārṣasaṃyutāḥ //
1.56.d:
गणयेत्संख्यया चैकनाड्यां मृत्युर्न पार्श्वयोः ।
प्राजापत्यब्राह्मदैवा विवाहाश्चार्षसंयुताः ॥
1.56.m: one should calculate by number: there is death in the same channel, but not at the sides. / The Prājāpatya, Brāhma, Daiva, and Ārṣa marriages—

1.56.s:
uktakāle tu kartavyāścatvāraḥ phaladāyakāḥ /
gandharvāsurapaiśācarākṣasākhyāstu sarvadā //
1.56.d:
उक्तकाले तु कर्तव्याश्चत्वारः फलदायकाः ।
गन्धर्वासुरपैशाचराक्षसाख्यास्तु सर्वदा ॥
1.56.m: these four, which grant good fruit, must be performed at the prescribed time; / but those called Gāndharva, Āsura, Paiśāca, and Rākṣasa may be performed at any time.

1.56.s:
caturthamabhijillagnamudayarkṣāñca saptamam /
godhūlikaṃ tadubhayaṃ vivāhe putrapautradam //
1.56.d:
चतुर्थमभिजिल्लग्नमुदयर्क्षाञ्च सप्तमम् ।
गोधूलिकं तदुभयं विवाहे पुत्रपौत्रदम् ॥
1.56.m: The fourth ascendant, Abhijit, and the seventh from the rising asterism, / is the twilight ascendant; both grant sons and grandsons in marriage.

1.56.s:
prācyā na ca kaliṅgānāṃ mukhyaṃ godhūlikaṃ smṛtam /
abhijitsarvadeśeṣu mukhyo doṣavināśakṛt //
1.56.d:
प्राच्या न च कलिङ्गानां मुख्यं गोधूलिकं स्मृतम् ।
अभिजित्सर्वदेशेषु मुख्यो दोषविनाशकृत् ॥
1.56.m: The twilight ascendant is not considered primary by easterners or the people of Kaliṅga; / Abhijit is primary in all countries, destroying defects.

1.56.s:
madhyandinagate bhānau muhūrto 'bhijidāhvayaḥ /
nāśayatyakhilāndoṣānpinākī tripuraṃ yathā //
1.56.d:
मध्यन्दिनगते भानौ मुहूर्तो ऽभिजिदाह्वयः ।
नाशयत्यखिलान्दोषान्पिनाकी त्रिपुरं यथा ॥
1.56.m: When the sun has reached midday, the muhūrta named Abhijit / destroys all defects, just as the bearer of Pināka [destroyed] Tripura.

1.56.s:
putrodvāhātparaṃ putrīvivāho na ṛtutraye /
na tayorvratamudvāhānmaṅgale nānyamaṅgalam //
1.56.d:
पुत्रोद्वाहात्परं पुत्रीविवाहो न ऋतुत्रये ।
न तयोर्व्रतमुद्वाहान्मङ्गले नान्यमङ्गलम् ॥
1.56.m: A daughter's marriage should not take place within three seasons after a son's wedding; / their tonsure or sacred-thread investiture should not occur after marriage; one auspicious rite must not follow upon another.

1.56.s:
vivāhaścaikajanyānāṃ ṣaṇmāsābhyantare yadi /
asaṃśayaṃ tribhirvarṣaistatraikā vidhavā bhavet //
1.56.d:
विवाहश्चैकजन्यानां षण्मासाभ्यन्तरे यदि ।
असंशयं त्रिभिर्वर्षैस्तत्रैका विधवा भवेत् ॥
1.56.m: If a marriage of those born of the same parents occurs within six months, / then without doubt, within three years one [of the brides] becomes a widow.

1.56.s:
pratyudvāho naiva kāryo naikasmai duhitṛdvayam /
na caikajanyayoḥ puṃsorekajanye tu kanyake //
1.56.d:
प्रत्युद्वाहो नैव कार्यो नैकस्मै दुहितृद्वयम् ।
न चैकजन्ययोः पुंसोरेकजन्ये तु कन्यके ॥
1.56.m: A cross-marriage should never be done, nor two daughters [given] to one man, / nor two daughters born of the same mother [given] to two men born of the same parents.

1.56.s:
naivaṃ kadācidudvāho naikadā muṇḍanadvayam /
divājātastu pitaraṃ rātrau tu jananīṃ tathā //
1.56.d:
नैवं कदाचिदुद्वाहो नैकदा मुण्डनद्वयम् ।
दिवाजातस्तु पितरं रात्रौ तु जननीं तथा ॥
1.56.m: Never should such a marriage be held, nor two tonsures at one time. / A child born in the day slays the father, and one born at night slays the mother;

1.56.s:
ātmānaṃ saṃdhyayorhanti nāsti gaṇḍe viparyayaḥ /
sutaḥ sutā vā niyataṃ śvasuraṃ hṝnti mūlajaḥ //
1.56.d:
आत्मानं संध्ययोर्हन्ति नास्ति गण्डे विपर्ययः ।
सुतः सुता वा नियतं श्वसुरं हॄन्ति मूलजः ॥
1.56.m: at the two twilights, it slays itself; there is no alteration in the Gaṇḍa junction. / A son or daughter born under Mūla definitely destroys the father-in-law;

1.56.s:
tadantyapādajo naiva tathāśleṣādyapādajaḥ /
jyeṣṭāntyapādajau jyeṣṭaṃ bālo hṝnti na bālikā //
1.56.d:
तदन्त्यपादजो नैव तथाश्लेषाद्यपादजः ।
ज्येष्टान्त्यपादजौ ज्येष्टं बालो हॄन्ति न बालिका ॥
1.56.m: but not if born in its last quarter; likewise, one born in the first quarter of Āśleṣā [destroys the mother-in-law]. / Born in the last quarter of Jyeṣṭhā, a boy destroys the elder brother, but not a girl.

1.56.s:
na bālikāṃbumūlarkṣe mātaraṃ pitaraṃ tathā /
saindrī dhavāgrajaṃ hṝnti devaraṃ tu dvidaivajā //
1.56.d:
न बालिकांबुमूलर्क्षे मातरं पितरं तथा ।
सैन्द्री धवाग्रजं हॄन्ति देवरं तु द्विदैवजा ॥
1.56.m: a girl born under Āśleṣā or Pūrvāṣāḍhā slays the mother and likewise the father. / A girl born under Jyeṣṭhā slays the elder brother of the husband, and one born under Viśākhā slays the husband's younger brother.

1.56.s:
ārabhyodvāhadivasāt ṣaṣṭe vāpyaṣṭame dine /
vadhūpraveśa saṃpattyaidaśame saptame dine //
1.56.d:
आरभ्योद्वाहदिवसात् षष्टे वाप्यष्टमे दिने ।
वधूप्रवेश संपत्त्यैदशमे सप्तमे दिने ॥
1.56.m: Beginning from the day of the marriage, on the sixth or on the eighth day, / on the tenth or on the seventh day, the entrance of the bride is for prosperity.

1.56.s:
hāyanadvitayaṃ janmabhalagnadivasānapi /
saṃtyajya hyatiśukre 'pi yātrā vaivāhikī śubhā //
1.56.d:
हायनद्वितयं जन्मभलग्नदिवसानपि ।
संत्यज्य ह्यतिशुक्रे ऽपि यात्रा वैवाहिकी शुभा ॥
1.56.m: Even when Venus is set, having avoided two years, / and also the days of the birth-constellation and ascendant, the marital journey is auspicious.

1.56.s:
śrīpradaṃ sarvagīrvāṇasthāpanaṃ cottarāyaṇe /
gīrvāṇapūrvagīrvāṇamatriṇordṛśyamānayoḥ //
1.56.d:
श्रीप्रदं सर्वगीर्वाणस्थापनं चोत्तरायणे ।
गीर्वाणपूर्वगीर्वाणमत्रिणोर्दृश्यमानयोः ॥
1.56.m: The installation of all gods during the northern course of the sun brings prosperity, / when Jupiter and Venus are visible,

1.56.s:
vicaitreṣveva māseṣu māghādiṣu ca pañcasu /
śuklapakṣeṣu kṛṣṇeṣu tadādiṣvaṣṭasu śubham //
1.56.d:
विचैत्रेष्वेव मासेषु माघादिषु च पञ्चसु ।
शुक्लपक्षेषु कृष्णेषु तदादिष्वष्टसु शुभम् ॥
1.56.m: in the months other than Caitra, namely in the five beginning with Māgha, / in the bright fortnights, and in the dark fortnights auspiciously in the eight [lunar days] beginning with the first,

1.56.s:
dineṣu yasya devasya yā titistatra tasya ca /
dvatīyādidvaye pañcamyāditastisṛṣu kramāt //
1.56.d:
दिनेषु यस्य देवस्य या तितिस्तत्र तस्य च ।
द्वतीयादिद्वये पञ्चम्यादितस्तिसृषु क्रमात् ॥
1.56.m: on the days and lunar day proper to whichever god [is being installed]; / in order, in the two beginning with the second, in the three beginning with the fifth,

1.56.s:
daśamyādeṣcatasṛṣu paurṇamāsyāṃ viśeṣataḥ /
tryuttarāditicandrāntyahastatrayagurūḍuṣu //
1.56.d:
दशम्यादेष्चतसृषु पौर्णमास्यां विशेषतः ।
त्र्युत्तरादितिचन्द्रान्त्यहस्तत्रयगुरूडुषु ॥
1.56.m: in the four beginning with the tenth, and especially on the full moon day; / under the asterisms of the three Uttarās, Punarvasu, Revatī, Hasta, Citrā, Svātī, and Puṣya,

1.56.s:
sāśvidhātṛjalādhīśaharimitravasuṣvapi /
kujavarjitavāreṣu kartuḥ sūrye balaprade //
1.56.d:
साश्विधातृजलाधीशहरिमित्रवसुष्वपि ।
कुजवर्जितवारेषु कर्तुः सूर्ये बलप्रदे ॥
1.56.m: along with Aśvinī, Rohiṇī, Pūrvāṣāḍhā, Śravaṇa, Anurādhā, and Dhaniṣṭhā, / on weekdays excluding Tuesday, when the Sun grants strength to the agent,

1.56.s:
candratārābalopete pūrvāhne śobhane dine /
śubhalagne śubhāṃśe ca kartturna nidhanodaye //
1.56.d:
चन्द्रताराबलोपेते पूर्वाह्ने शोभने दिने ।
शुभलग्ने शुभांशे च कर्त्तुर्न निधनोदये ॥
1.56.m: endowed with the strength of the Moon and the stars, in the forenoon of an auspicious day, / in an auspicious ascendant and auspicious divisional degree, when the eighth sign does not rise for the agent.

1.56.s:
rāśayaḥ sakalāḥ śreṣṭhāḥ śubhagrahayutekṣitāḥ /
pañcāṣṭake śubhe lagne naidhane śuddhisaṃyute //
1.56.d:
राशयः सकलाः श्रेष्ठाः शुभग्रहयुतेक्षिताः ।
पञ्चाष्टके शुभे लग्ने नैधने शुद्धिसंयुते ॥
1.56.m: All signs are excellent when conjoined with or aspected by benefic planets; / in an auspicious ascendant with five and eight [benefics], and the eighth house endowed with purity.

1.56.s:
lagnasthāścandrasūryārarāhuketvarkasūnavaḥ /
kartturmṛtyupradāścānye dhanadhānyasukhapradāḥ //
1.56.d:
लग्नस्थाश्चन्द्रसूर्यारराहुकेत्वर्कसूनवः ।
कर्त्तुर्मृत्युप्रदाश्चान्ये धनधान्यसुखप्रदाः ॥
1.56.m: The Moon, Sun, Mars, Rāhu, Ketu, and Saturn situated in the ascendant / cause death to the agent; the others grant wealth, grain, and happiness.

1.56.s:
dvitīye neṣṭadāḥ pāpāḥ saumyāścandraścaḥ vittadāḥ /
tṛtīye nikhilāḥ kheṭāḥ putrapautrasukhapradāḥ //
1.56.d:
द्वितीये नेष्टदाः पापाः सौम्याश्चन्द्रश्चः वित्तदाः ।
तृतीये निखिलाः खेटाः पुत्रपौत्रसुखप्रदाः ॥
1.56.m: Malefics in the second house do not give desired results; benefics and the Moon give wealth. / In the third house, all planets give the happiness of sons and grandsons.

1.56.s:
caturthe sukhadāḥ saumyāḥ krūrāḥ kheṭāśca duḥkhadāḥ /
glānidāḥ pañcame krūrāḥ saumyāḥ putrasukhapradāḥ //
1.56.d:
चतुर्थे सुखदाः सौम्याः क्रूराः खेटाश्च दुःखदाः ।
ग्लानिदाः पञ्चमे क्रूराः सौम्याः पुत्रसुखप्रदाः ॥
1.56.m: In the fourth, benefics give happiness, and cruel planets cause misery. / In the fifth, cruel planets cause debility; benefics give the happiness of sons.

1.56.s:
ṣaṣṭe śubhāḥ śatrudāḥ syuḥ pāpāḥ śabrukṣayaṅkarāḥ /
vyādhidāḥ saptame pāpāḥ saumyāḥ śubhaphalapradāḥ //
1.56.d:
षष्टे शुभाः शत्रुदाः स्युः पापाः शब्रुक्षयङ्कराः ।
व्याधिदाः सप्तमे पापाः सौम्याः शुभफलप्रदाः ॥
1.56.m: In the sixth, benefics cause enemies; malefics bring about the destruction of enemies. / In the seventh, malefics bring disease; benefics grant auspicious results.

1.56.s:
aṣṭamasthāḥ khagāḥ sarvekarturmṛtyupradāyakāḥ /
dharme pāpā ghnanti saumyāḥ śubhadā maṅgalapradāḥ //
1.56.d:
अष्टमस्थाः खगाः सर्वेकर्तुर्मृत्युप्रदायकाः ।
धर्मे पापा घ्नन्ति सौम्याः शुभदा मङ्गलप्रदाः ॥
1.56.m: All planets situated in the eighth house bring about death for the agent. / In the ninth, malefics destroy; benefics bring auspiciousness and grant prosperity.

1.56.s:
karmagā duḥkhadāḥ pāpā saumyāścandraśca kīrtidāḥ /
lābhasthānagatāḥ sarve bhūrilābhapradā grahāḥ //
1.56.d:
कर्मगा दुःखदाः पापा सौम्याश्चन्द्रश्च कीर्तिदाः ।
लाभस्थानगताः सर्वे भूरिलाभप्रदा ग्रहाः ॥
1.56.m: In the tenth, malefics cause misery; benefics and the Moon grant fame. / All planets situated in the house of gain (the eleventh) bestow abundant gain.

1.56.s:
vyayasthānagatāḥ śaśvadbahūvyayakarā grahāḥ /
hṝntyarthahīnāḥ kartāraṃ mantrahīnāstu ṛtvijam //
sriyaṃ lakṣaṇahīnāstu na pratiṣṭāsamo ripuḥ //
1.56.d:
व्ययस्थानगताः शश्वद्बहूव्ययकरा ग्रहाः ।
हॄन्त्यर्थहीनाः कर्तारं मन्त्रहीनास्तु ऋत्विजम् ॥
स्रियं लक्षणहीनास्तु न प्रतिष्टासमो रिपुः ॥
1.56.m:
Planets situated in the house of expenditure (the twelfth) constantly cause great expenditure. / [Rites] devoid of wealth destroy the patron, while those devoid of mantra destroy the officiating priest;

[rites] devoid of correct marks destroy fortune; there is no enemy like a faulty consecration.

1.56.s: guṇādhikatare lagne doṣaḥ svalpataro yadi //
1.56.d: गुणाधिकतरे लग्ने दोषः स्वल्पतरो यदि ॥
1.56.m: If in an ascendant possessing an excess of merits there is a very small fault,

1.56.s:
surāṇāṃ sthāpanaṃ tatra karturiṣṭārthasiddhidam /
nirmāṇāyatanagrāmagṛhādīnāṃ samāsataḥ //
1.56.d:
सुराणां स्थापनं तत्र कर्तुरिष्टार्थसिद्धिदम् ।
निर्माणायतनग्रामगृहादीनां समासतः ॥
1.56.m: the installation of the gods therein accomplishes the desired goal for the agent. / In brief, for the construction of temples, villages, houses, and the like:

1.56.s:
kṣetramādau parīkṣeta gandhavarṇarasāṃśakaiḥ /
madhupuṣpāmlapiśitagandhaṃ viprānupūrvakam //
1.56.d:
क्षेत्रमादौ परीक्षेत गन्धवर्णरसांशकैः ।
मधुपुष्पाम्लपिशितगन्धं विप्रानुपूर्वकम् ॥
1.56.m: One should first examine the ground by smell, color, taste, and portions: / having the smell of honey, flower, sour gruel, or flesh, in the order of the brāhmaṇas and other [castes];

1.56.s:
sitaṃ raktaṃ ca haritaṃ kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ yathākramam /
madhuraṃ kaṭukaṃ tiktaṃ kaṣāyakarasaṃ kramāt //
1.56.d:
सितं रक्तं च हरितं कृष्णवर्णं यथाक्रमम् ।
मधुरं कटुकं तिक्तं कषायकरसं क्रमात् ॥
1.56.m: white, red, yellow, and black in color in due order; / sweet, pungent, bitter, and astringent in taste respectively.

1.56.s:
atyantavṛddhidaṃ nṝṇāmīśānaprāgudagplavam /
anyadikṣu plave teṣāṃ śaśvadatyantahānidam //
1.56.d:
अत्यन्तवृद्धिदं नॄणामीशानप्रागुदग्प्लवम् ।
अन्यदिक्षु प्लवे तेषां शश्वदत्यन्तहानिदम् ॥
1.56.m: A ground sloping toward the northeast, east, or north brings immense prosperity to men; / a slope toward other directions constantly brings immense loss to them.

1.56.s:
samagartāratnimātraṃ khanitvā tatra pūrayet /
atyantavṛddhiradhike hīne hāniḥ same samam //
1.56.d:
समगर्तारत्निमात्रं खनित्वा तत्र पूरयेत् ।
अत्यन्तवृद्धिरधिके हीने हानिः समे समम् ॥
1.56.m: Having dug an even pit measuring one cubit, one should refill it with that [earth]; / if there is excess, there is immense prosperity; if a deficit, loss; if equal, neutrality.

1.56.s:
tathā niśādau tatkṛtvā pānīyena prapūrayet /
prātardṛṣṭe jale vṛddhiḥ samaṃ paṅke kṣayaḥ kṣaye //
1.56.d:
तथा निशादौ तत्कृत्वा पानीयेन प्रपूरयेत् ।
प्रातर्दृष्टे जले वृद्धिः समं पङ्के क्षयः क्षये ॥
1.56.m: Likewise, having done that at the beginning of night, one should fill it with water. / If water is seen in the morning, there is prosperity; if mud, mediocrity; if it has diminished, ruin.

1.56.s:
evaṃ lakṣaṇasaṃyuktaṃ samyak kṣetraṃ samīkṣyate /
diksādhanāya tanmadhye samaṃ maṇḍalamālikhet //
1.56.d:
एवं लक्षणसंयुक्तं सम्यक् क्षेत्रं समीक्ष्यते ।
दिक्साधनाय तन्मध्ये समं मण्डलमालिखेत् ॥
1.56.m: Thus the plot endowed with proper characteristics is thoroughly examined. / To ascertain the directions, one should draw a level circle in its center.

1.56.s:
dvādaśāṅgulakaṃ śaṅkuṃ sthāpyekṣettatra diktramam /
caturasrīkṛte kṣetre ṣaḍvargapariśodhite //
1.56.d:
द्वादशाङ्गुलकं शङ्कुं स्थाप्येक्षेत्तत्र दिक्त्रमम् ।
चतुरस्रीकृते क्षेत्रे षड्वर्गपरिशोधिते ॥
1.56.m: Setting up a gnomon of twelve fingers, one should observe therein the course of the directions. / On a site made square and purified by the six astrological criteria,

1.56.s:
rekhāmārge ca karttavyaṃ prākāraṃ sumanoharam /
āyāmeṣu caturdikṣu prāgādiṣu ca satsvapi //
1.56.d:
रेखामार्गे च कर्त्तव्यं प्राकारं सुमनोहरम् ।
आयामेषु चतुर्दिक्षु प्रागादिषु च सत्स्वपि ॥
1.56.m: an exceedingly charming boundary wall should be built along the line. / In the extensions along the four directions, beginning with the east,

1.56.s:
aṣṭāvaṣṭau pratidiśaṃ dvārāṇi syuryathākramam /
pradakṣiṇakramātteṣāmamūni ca phalāni vai //
1.56.d:
अष्टावष्टौ प्रतिदिशं द्वाराणि स्युर्यथाक्रमम् ।
प्रदक्षिणक्रमात्तेषाममूनि च फलानि वै ॥
1.56.m: there should be eight doors in each direction in proper sequence. / In clockwise order, their results are indeed these:

1.56.s:
hānirnaiḥ khyandhanaprāptirnṛpapūjā mahadvanam /
aticauryamatikrodho bhītirdiśi śacīpateḥ //
1.56.d:
हानिर्नैः ख्यन्धनप्राप्तिर्नृपपूजा महद्वनम् ।
अतिचौर्यमतिक्रोधो भीतिर्दिशि शचीपतेः ॥
1.56.m: Loss, fame, acquisition of wealth, royal honor, great forest, / extreme theft, extreme anger, and fear in the direction of Indra;

1.56.s:
nidhanaṃ bandhanaṃ bhītirarthāptirddhanavarddhanam /
anāntakaṃ vyādhibhayaṃ niḥsattvaṃ dakṣiṇādiśi //
1.56.d:
निधनं बन्धनं भीतिरर्थाप्तिर्द्धनवर्द्धनम् ।
अनान्तकं व्याधिभयं निःसत्त्वं दक्षिणादिशि ॥
1.56.m: death, imprisonment, fear, gain of purpose, increase of wealth, / immortality, fear of disease, and weakness in the southern direction;

1.56.s:
putrahāniḥ śatruvṛddhirlakṣmīprāptirddhanāgamaḥ /
saubhāgyamatidaurbhāgyaṃ duḥkhaṃ śokaśca paścime //
1.56.d:
पुत्रहानिः शत्रुवृद्धिर्लक्ष्मीप्राप्तिर्द्धनागमः ।
सौभाग्यमतिदौर्भाग्यं दुःखं शोकश्च पश्चिमे ॥
1.56.m: loss of sons, increase of enemies, attainment of fortune, arrival of wealth, / good fortune, great misfortune, misery, and grief in the west;

1.56.s:
kalatrahānirniḥ sattvaṃ hānirddhānyadhanāgamaḥ /
saṃpadvṛddhirmāsabhītirāmayaṃ diśi śītagoḥ //
1.56.d:
कलत्रहानिर्निः सत्त्वं हानिर्द्धान्यधनागमः ।
संपद्वृद्धिर्मासभीतिरामयं दिशि शीतगोः ॥
1.56.m: loss of a wife, weakness, loss, arrival of grain and wealth, / increase of prosperity, fear of months, and sickness in the direction of the Moon.

1.56.s:
evaṃ gṛhādiṣu dvāravistārāddviguṇocchritam /
paścime dakṣiṇe vāpi kapāṭaṃ sthāpayedgṛhe //
1.56.d:
एवं गृहादिषु द्वारविस्ताराद्द्विगुणोच्छ्रितम् ।
पश्चिमे दक्षिणे वापि कपाटं स्थापयेद्गृहे ॥
1.56.m: Thus, in houses and the like, twice as high as the width of the door, / one should place the door-panel in the house, either in the west or in the south.

1.56.s:
prākārāntaḥ kṣitiṃ kuryādekāśītipadaṃ yathā /
madhye navapade brahmasthānaṃ tadatininditam //
1.56.d:
प्राकारान्तः क्षितिं कुर्यादेकाशीतिपदं यथा ।
मध्ये नवपदे ब्रह्मस्थानं तदतिनिन्दितम् ॥
1.56.m: Inside the enclosure, one should make the ground into eighty-one squares; / in the center, on nine squares, is the place of Brahmā, which is extremely forbidden [for building].

1.56.s:
dvātriṃśadaṃśāḥ prākārasamīyāṃśāḥ samantataḥ /
piśācāṃśe gṛhāraṃbhe duḥkhaśokabhayapradaḥ //
1.56.d:
द्वात्रिंशदंशाः प्राकारसमीयांशाः समन्ततः ।
पिशाचांशे गृहारंभे दुःखशोकभयप्रदः ॥
1.56.m: Thirty-two divisions are the border divisions all around; / beginning a house in the piśāca division brings misery, grief, and fear.

1.56.s:
śeṣāśāḥ syuśca nirmāṇe putrapautradhanapradāḥ /
śirāḥ syurvāstunorekhā digvidigmadhyasaṃbhavāḥ //
1.56.d:
शेषाशाः स्युश्च निर्माणे पुत्रपौत्रधनप्रदाः ।
शिराः स्युर्वास्तुनोरेखा दिग्विदिग्मध्यसंभवाः ॥
1.56.m: The remaining divisions for construction give sons, grandsons, and wealth. / The channels are lines of the building-site originating from the center of the cardinal and intermediate directions.

1.56.s:
brahmabhāgāḥ piśācāṃśāḥ śirāṇāṃ yatra saṃhatiḥ /
tatra tatra vijānīyādvāstuno marmasaṃdhayaḥ //
1.56.d:
ब्रह्मभागाः पिशाचांशाः शिराणां यत्र संहतिः ।
तत्र तत्र विजानीयाद्वास्तुनो मर्मसंधयः ॥
1.56.m: The portions of Brahmā and the piśāca portions, wherever there is a junction of the channels, / in each such place one should know the vital points and joints of the building-site.

1.56.s:
marmāṇi saṃdhayo neṣṭāḥ svasthe 'pyevaṃ niveśane /
saumyaphaālgunavaiśākhamāghaśrāvaṇakārtikāḥ //
1.56.d:
मर्माणि संधयो नेष्टाः स्वस्थे ऽप्येवं निवेशने ।
सौम्यफआल्गुनवैशाखमाघश्रावणकार्तिकाः ॥
1.56.m: Vital points and joints are not desired even in a well-situated dwelling. / Mārgaśīrṣa, Phālguna, Vaiśākha, Māgha, Śrāvaṇa, and Kārttika

1.56.s:
māsāḥ syurgṛhanirmāṇe putrārogyadhanapradāḥ /
akārādiṣu bhāgṣu dikṣu prāgādiṣu kramāt //
1.56.d:
मासाः स्युर्गृहनिर्माणे पुत्रारोग्यधनप्रदाः ।
अकारादिषु भाग्षु दिक्षु प्रागादिषु क्रमात् ॥
1.56.m: are months in house-construction that grant sons, health, and wealth. / In the divisions beginning with the sound 'a', in the directions beginning with the east in order,

1.56.s:
kharośvotha hariḥ śvākhyaḥ sapokhugajaśāśakāḥ /
digvargāṇāmiyaṃ yoniḥ svavargātpañcamo ripuḥ //
1.56.d:
खरोश्वोथ हरिः श्वाख्यः सपोखुगजशाशकाः ।
दिग्वर्गाणामियं योनिः स्ववर्गात्पञ्चमो रिपुः ॥
1.56.m: are the donkey, horse, lion, dog, snake, rat, elephant, and hare. / This is the origin of the direction-groups; the fifth from one's own group is an enemy.

1.56.s:
sādhyavargaḥ puraḥ sthāpya pṛṣṭataḥ sādhakaṃ nyaset /
vyatyaye nāśanaṃ tasya ṛṇamadhyaṃ dhanācchubham //
1.56.d:
साध्यवर्गः पुरः स्थाप्य पृष्टतः साधकं न्यसेत् ।
व्यत्यये नाशनं तस्य ऋणमध्यं धनाच्छुभम् ॥
1.56.m: One should place the target-group in front and set the practitioner-group behind; / in the reverse, there is destruction; a middle debt is auspicious from wealth.

1.56.s:
ārabhya sādhakaṃ ghiṣṇyaṃ sādhyaṃ yāvaccaturguṇam /
vibhejetsaptabhiḥ śeṣaṃ sādhakasya dhanaṃ tadā //
1.56.d:
आरभ्य साधकं घिष्ण्यं साध्यं यावच्चतुर्गुणम् ।
विभेजेत्सप्तभिः शेषं साधकस्य धनं तदा ॥
1.56.m: Starting from the practitioner asterism up to the target, multiplied by four, / one should divide by seven; the remainder is then the wealth of the practitioner.

1.56.s:
vistāra āyāmaguṇo gṛhasya padamucyate /
tasmāddhanādhanāyarkṣavārāṃśāḥ saṃkhyayā kramāt //
1.56.d:
विस्तार आयामगुणो गृहस्य पदमुच्यते ।
तस्माद्धनाधनायर्क्षवारांशाः संख्यया क्रमात् ॥
1.56.m: The breadth multiplied by the length is called the square area of the house. / From that, wealth, non-wealth, asterism, and portions of the day are computed by number in due sequence.

1.56.s:
dhanādhikaṃ gṛhaṃ vṛddhyai ṛṇādhikamaśobhanam /
viṣamāyaḥ śubhaghāyaiva samāyo nirdhanāya ca //
1.56.d:
धनाधिकं गृहं वृद्ध्यै ऋणाधिकमशोभनम् ।
विषमायः शुभघायैव समायो निर्धनाय च ॥
1.56.m: A house with an excess of wealth brings prosperity; one with an excess of debt is inauspicious. / An odd income destroys good fortune, and an equal income leads to poverty.

1.56.s:
ghanakṣayastṛtīyarkṣe pañcamarkṣe paraḥ kṣayaḥ /
ātmakṣayaḥ saptamarkṣe bhavatyeva hi bhartṛbhāt //
1.56.d:
घनक्षयस्तृतीयर्क्षे पञ्चमर्क्षे परः क्षयः ।
आत्मक्षयः सप्तमर्क्षे भवत्येव हि भर्तृभात् ॥
1.56.m: In the third asterism there is loss of accumulated wealth; in the fifth asterism, great ruin; / and in the seventh asterism from the master's birth-star, destruction of self indeed occurs.

1.56.s:
dvirdvādaśo nirdhanāya trikoṇamasutāya ca /
ṣaṭkāṣṭakaṃ mṛtyave syācchubhadārāśayaḥ pare //
1.56.d:
द्विर्द्वादशो निर्धनाय त्रिकोणमसुताय च ।
षट्काष्टकं मृत्यवे स्याच्छुभदाराशयः परे ॥
1.56.m: The second and twelfth [positions] cause poverty; the trine causes childlessness; / the sixth and eighth cause death; the other signs are auspicious.

1.56.s:
sūryāṅgārakavārāṃśā vaiśvānarabhayapradāḥ /
itare grahavārāṃśāḥ sarvakāmārthasiddhidāḥ //
1.56.d:
सूर्याङ्गारकवारांशा वैश्वानरभयप्रदाः ।
इतरे ग्रहवारांशाः सर्वकामार्थसिद्धिदाः ॥
1.56.m: The day-divisions of the Sun and Mars cause danger from fire; / the day-divisions of the other planets grant the attainment of all desires and wealth.

1.56.s:
nabhasyādiṣu māseṣu triṣu triṣu yathākramam /
pūrvādikaśirovāmapārśveśāyāpradakṣiṇam //
1.56.d:
नभस्यादिषु मासेषु त्रिषु त्रिषु यथाक्रमम् ।
पूर्वादिकशिरोवामपार्श्वेशायाप्रदक्षिणम् ॥
1.56.m:
In three months each, beginning with Nabhasya in due order,
lying on the left side, [facing] the north-east, with the head towards the east and subsequent [directions] clockwise,

1.56.s:
carāhvayo vāstupumān caratyevaṃ mahodaraḥ /
yaddiṅmukho vāstupumān kuryāttaddiṅmukhaṃ gṛham //
1.56.d:
चराह्वयो वास्तुपुमान् चरत्येवं महोदरः ।
यद्दिङ्मुखो वास्तुपुमान् कुर्यात्तद्दिङ्मुखं गृहम् ॥
1.56.m:
the large-bellied site-man called Cara thus roams.
In whichever direction the site-man has his face turned, in that direction one should make the house face.

1.56.s:
pratikūlamukhaṃ gehaṃ rogaśokabhayapradam /
sabalo mukhagehānāmeṣa doṣo na vidyate //
1.56.d:
प्रतिकूलमुखं गेहं रोगशोकभयप्रदम् ।
सबलो मुखगेहानामेष दोषो न विद्यते ॥
1.56.m:
A house facing in the opposite direction brings disease, grief, and fear.
For a house that has a strong front, this defect is not found.

1.56.s:
vṛtyeṭikāṃ svarṇareṇudhānyaśaivalasaṃyutam /
gṛhamadhye hastamātre garte nyāsāya vinyaset //
1.56.d:
वृत्येटिकां स्वर्णरेणुधान्यशैवलसंयुतम् ।
गृहमध्ये हस्तमात्रे गर्ते न्यासाय विन्यसेत् ॥
1.56.m:
Along with an enclosed brick, gold dust, grain, and algae,
one should place [them] for deposit in a pit measuring one cubit in the centre of the house.

1.56.s:
vastvāyāmadalaṃ nābhistasmādadhyaṅgulatrayam /
kukṣistasminnyasecchaṅkuṃ putrapautravivardhanam //
1.56.d:
वस्त्वायामदलं नाभिस्तस्मादध्यङ्गुलत्रयम् ।
कुक्षिस्तस्मिन्न्यसेच्छङ्कुं पुत्रपौत्रविवर्धनम् ॥
1.56.m:
Half of the length of the site is the navel; three aṅgulas above that
is the belly; there one should drive the peg that causes sons and grandsons to flourish.

1.56.s:
caturviśatrayorviṃśatṣoḍaśadvādaśāṅgulaiḥ /
viprādīnāṃ kukṣimānaṃ svarṇavastrādyalaṅkṛtam //
1.56.d:
चतुर्विशत्रयोर्विंशत्षोडशद्वादशाङ्गुलैः ।
विप्रादीनां कुक्षिमानं स्वर्णवस्त्राद्यलङ्कृतम् ॥
1.56.m:
By twenty-four, twenty-three, sixteen, and twelve aṅgulas
is the belly measurement for Brahmins and the others, adorned with gold, cloth, and so on.

1.56.s:
khadirārjunaśālotthaṃ yugayantraṃ tarūdbhaghavam /
raktacandanapālāśaraktaśānaviśālajam //
1.56.d:
खदिरार्जुनशालोत्थं युगयन्त्रं तरूद्भघवम् ।
रक्तचन्दनपालाशरक्तशानविशालजम् ॥
1.56.m:
Produced from Khadira, Arjuna, or Śāla, a balanced peg born of trees,
or made of red sandalwood, Palāśa, or broad Raktaśāna,

1.56.s:
śakuṃ tridhā vibhajyāndyaṃ caturasraṃ tataḥ param /
aṣṭāsraṃ ca tṛtīyāsau manvasraṃ mṛdumavraṇam //
1.56.d:
शकुं त्रिधा विभज्यान्द्यं चतुरस्रं ततः परम् ।
अष्टास्रं च तृतीयासौ मन्वस्रं मृदुमव्रणम् ॥
1.56.m:
having divided the peg into three parts: the first four-sided, following that
eight-sided, and the third fourteen-sided, smooth and free from blemishes—

1.56.s:
evaṃ lakṣaṇasaṃyuktaṃ parikalpya śubhe dine /
ṣaḍvargaśuddhisūtreṇa sūtrite dharaṇītale //
1.56.d:
एवं लक्षणसंयुक्तं परिकल्प्य शुभे दिने ।
षड्वर्गशुद्धिसूत्रेण सूत्रिते धरणीतले ॥
1.56.m:
having thus fashioned it endowed with [auspicious] characteristics on an auspicious day,
when the ground has been marked out with the string purified by the six astrological divisions,

1.56.s:
mṛdudhruvakṣiprabheṣu riktāmāvarjite dine /
vyarkāracaralagneṣu pāpe cāṣṭamavarjite //
1.56.d:
मृदुध्रुवक्षिप्रभेषु रिक्तामावर्जिते दिने ।
व्यर्कारचरलग्नेषु पापे चाष्टमवर्जिते ॥
1.56.m:
under mild, fixed, or swift asterisms, on a day free from Rikta [tithis] and the new moon,
in movable ascendants devoid of the Sun and Mars, and with malefics absent from the eighth house,

1.56.s:
naidhane śuddhisaṃyukte śubhaghalagne śubhāṃśake /
śubhekṣite 'tha vā yukte lagne śaṅkuṃ vinikṣipet //
1.56.d:
नैधने शुद्धिसंयुक्ते शुभघलग्ने शुभांशके ।
शुभेक्षिते ऽथ वा युक्ते लग्ने शङ्कुं विनिक्षिपेत् ॥
1.56.m:
when the eighth house is purified, in a benefic ascendant and a benefic navāṃśa,
aspected by or conjoined with a benefic in the ascendant, one should drive the peg.

1.56.s:
puṇyāhaghoṣairvāditraiḥ puṇyapuṇyāṅganādibhiḥ /
svatrikendratrikoṇasthaiḥ śubhaistryāyārigaiḥ paraiḥ //
1.56.d:
पुण्याहघोषैर्वादित्रैः पुण्यपुण्याङ्गनादिभिः ।
स्वत्रिकेन्द्रत्रिकोणस्थैः शुभैस्त्र्यायारिगैः परैः ॥
1.56.m:
Accompanied by proclamations of auspicious days, musical instruments, and blessed chaste women,
with benefics situated in their own trines, angles, and trines, and the other [malefics] situated in the third, eleventh, and sixth houses,

1.56.s:
lagnāṃśāṣṭāricandreṇa daivajñārcanapūrvakam /
ekadvitricatuḥśālāḥ sapta śālā daśāhvayāḥ //
1.56.d:
लग्नांशाष्टारिचन्द्रेण दैवज्ञार्चनपूर्वकम् ।
एकद्वित्रिचतुःशालाः सप्त शाला दशाह्वयाः ॥
1.56.m:
with the Moon in the ascendant's navāṃśa, the eighth, or the sixth, preceded by the worship of the astrologer:
there are houses of one, two, three, and four halls, seven halls, and those called ten [halls].

1.56.s:
tāḥ punaḥ ṣaḍvidhāḥ śālāḥ pratyekaṃ daśaṣaḍvidhāḥ /
dhruvaṃ dhānyaṃ jayaṃ nandaṃ kharaḥ kāntaṃ manoramam //
1.56.d:
ताः पुनः षड्विधाः शालाः प्रत्येकं दशषड्विधाः ।
ध्रुवं धान्यं जयं नन्दं खरः कान्तं मनोरमम् ॥
1.56.m:
Those halls are again of six kinds, each being of sixteen kinds:
Dhruva, Dhānya, Jaya, Nanda, Khara, Kānta, Manorama,

1.56.s:
sumukhaṃ durmukhaṃ krūraṃ śatruṃ svarṇapradaṃ kṣayam /
ākrandaṃ vipulākhya ca vijayaṃ ṣoḍaśaṃ gṛham //
1.56.d:
सुमुखं दुर्मुखं क्रूरं शत्रुं स्वर्णप्रदं क्षयम् ।
आक्रन्दं विपुलाख्य च विजयं षोडशं गृहम् ॥
1.56.m:
Sumukha, Durmukha, Krūra, Śatru, Svarṇaprada, Kṣaya,
Ākranda, the one named Vipula, and the sixteenth house, Vijaya.

1.56.s:
gṛhāṇi gaṇayedevaṃ teṣāṃ prastārabhedataḥ /
guroragho laghuḥ sthāpyaḥ purastādūrdhvavannyaset //
1.56.d:
गृहाणि गणयेदेवं तेषां प्रस्तारभेदतः ।
गुरोरघो लघुः स्थाप्यः पुरस्तादूर्ध्ववन्न्यसेत् ॥
1.56.m:
One should calculate the houses in this manner through the permutations of their distribution:
a light [syllable] is to be placed below a heavy [syllable]; in front, one should place it as above;

1.56.s:
gurubhiḥ pūrayetpaścātsarvaladhvavadhīrvidhiḥ /
kuryāllaghupade 'lindaṃ gṛhadvārātpradakṣiṇam //
1.56.d:
गुरुभिः पूरयेत्पश्चात्सर्वलध्ववधीर्विधिः ।
कुर्याल्लघुपदे ऽलिन्दं गृहद्वारात्प्रदक्षिणम् ॥
1.56.m:
one should fill [the rest] behind with heavy [syllables]—this rule holds until all are light.
In the place of a light [syllable], one should make a veranda clockwise from the door of the house.

1.56.s:
pūrvādigeṣvalindeṣu gṛhabhedāstu ṣoḍaśa /
snānāgāraṃ diśi prācyāmāgneyyāṃ pākamandiram //
1.56.d:
पूर्वादिगेष्वलिन्देषु गृहभेदास्तु षोडश ।
स्नानागारं दिशि प्राच्यामाग्नेय्यां पाकमन्दिरम् ॥
1.56.m:
With the verandas facing the east and other directions, there are sixteen varieties of houses:
the bathhouse in the eastern quarter; in the south-east, the kitchen;

1.56.s:
yāmyāṃ ca śayanāgāraṃ nairṛtyāṃ śāsramandiram /
pratīcyāṃ bhojanagṛhaṃ vā yavyāṃ dhānyamadiram //
1.56.d:
याम्यां च शयनागारं नैरृत्यां शास्रमन्दिरम् ।
प्रतीच्यां भोजनगृहं वा यव्यां धान्यमदिरम् ॥
1.56.m:
in the south, the bedroom; in the south-west, the armoury;
in the west, the dining room; in the north-west, the granary;

1.56.s:
kauberyāṃ devatāgāramīśānyāṃ kṣiramandiram /
śayyāmūtrāstratadvicca bhojanaṃ maṅgalāśrayam //
dhānyastrībhogavittaṃ ca śṛṅgārāyatanāni ca ///
1.56.d:
कौबेर्यां देवतागारमीशान्यां क्षिरमन्दिरम् ।
शय्यामूत्रास्त्रतद्विच्च भोजनं मङ्गलाश्रयम् ॥
धान्यस्त्रीभोगवित्तं च शृङ्गारायतनानि च ॥।

1.56.s: īśānyādikramasteṣāṃ gṛhanirmāṇakaṃ śubham //
1.56.d: ईशान्यादिक्रमस्तेषां गृहनिर्माणकं शुभम् ॥
1.56.m: their construction of the house in the order beginning with the north-east is auspicious.

1.56.s:
eteṣvetāni śastrāṇi svaṃ sthāpyāni svadikṣvapi /
dhvajo dhūmrotha siṃhaḥ śvā saurameyaḥ kharo gajāḥ //
1.56.d:
एतेष्वेतानि शस्त्राणि स्वं स्थाप्यानि स्वदिक्ष्वपि ।
ध्वजो धूम्रोथ सिंहः श्वा सौरमेयः खरो गजाः ॥
1.56.m:
Among these, these auspicious [arrangements] are to be established in their own directions:
Dhvaja, Dhūmra, Siṃha, Śvan, Saurameya, Khara, Gaja,

1.56.s:
dhvāṅkṣaścaiva bhavantyaṣṭau pūrvādipāḥ kramādamī /
plakṣoduṃbaracūtākhyā niṃbastu hi vibhītakāḥ //
1.56.d:
ध्वाङ्क्षश्चैव भवन्त्यष्टौ पूर्वादिपाः क्रमादमी ।
प्लक्षोदुंबरचूताख्या निंबस्तु हि विभीतकाः ॥
1.56.m:
and Dhvāṅkṣa are the eight [ayas] that rule the directions beginning with the east, in order.
Plakṣa, Udumbara, the so-called Cūta, Nimba, and indeed Vibhītaka,

1.56.s:
ya kaṭakā dugdhavṛkṣā vṛkṣāśvatthakapitthakāḥ /
agastisiṃdhuvālākhyatintiḍīkāśca ninditāḥ //
1.56.d:
य कटका दुग्धवृक्षा वृक्षाश्वत्थकपित्थकाः ।
अगस्तिसिंधुवालाख्यतिन्तिडीकाश्च निन्दिताः ॥
1.56.m:
thorny [trees], milky trees, Aśvattha and Kapittha trees,
and those called Agasti, Sindhuvāra, and Tintiḍīka are censured.

1.56.s:
pittavāgrajadehasyātpaścime dakṣiṇe tathā /
gṛhapādāgṛhastabhāḥ samāḥ śastāśca nāsamāḥ //
1.56.d:
पित्तवाग्रजदेहस्यात्पश्चिमे दक्षिणे तथा ।
गृहपादागृहस्तभाः समाः शस्ताश्च नासमाः ॥
1.56.m:
They would cause bilious and windy disorders to the body in the west and in the south.
The supports and pillars of the house should be even and auspicious, not uneven.

1.56.s:
nātyucchritaṃ nātinīcaṃ kuḍyotsedhaṃ yathāruci /
gṛhopari gṛhādīnāmevaṃ sarvatra cintayet //
1.56.d:
नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं कुड्योत्सेधं यथारुचि ।
गृहोपरि गृहादीनामेवं सर्वत्र चिन्तयेत् ॥
1.56.m:
Neither too high nor too low, the height of the walls should be according to desire.
One should consider in this manner everywhere regarding a house above a house and so on.

1.56.s:
gṛhādīnāṃ gṛhaśrāvaṃ kramaśo 'ṣṭavidhaṃ smṛtam /
pāñcālamānaṃ vaidehaṃ kauravaṃ ca kujanyakam //
1.56.d:
गृहादीनां गृहश्रावं क्रमशो ऽष्टविधं स्मृतम् ।
पाञ्चालमानं वैदेहं कौरवं च कुजन्यकम् ॥
1.56.m:
The roof-slope of houses and the like is traditionally remembered to be of eight kinds in order:
the Pāñcāla measure, Vaideha, Kaurava, Kaujanyaka,

1.56.s:
māgadhaṃ śūrasenaṃ ca gāndhārāvatikā smṛtam /
sacaturbhāgavistāramutsedhaṃ yattaducyate //
1.56.d:
मागधं शूरसेनं च गान्धारावतिका स्मृतम् ।
सचतुर्भागविस्तारमुत्सेधं यत्तदुच्यते ॥
1.56.m:
Māgadha, Śūrasena, Gāndhāra, and Avantika.
The height which is stated to be four parts of the width,

1.56.s:
pāñcālamātulānāṃ ca hyuttarottaravṛddhitaḥ /
vaidehādīnyaśeṣāṇi mānāni syuryathākramam //
1.56.d:
पाञ्चालमातुलानां च ह्युत्तरोत्तरवृद्धितः ।
वैदेहादीन्यशेषाणि मानानि स्युर्यथाक्रमम् ॥
1.56.m:
through the successive increase of the Pāñcāla and the cross-beams,
would yield all the measures beginning with Vaideha in due order.

1.56.s:
pāñcālamānaṃ sarveṣāṃ sādhāraṇamataḥ param /
avantimānaṃ viprāṇāṃ gāndhāraṃ kṣatriyasya ca //
1.56.d:
पाञ्चालमानं सर्वेषां साधारणमतः परम् ।
अवन्तिमानं विप्राणां गान्धारं क्षत्रियस्य च ॥
1.56.m:
The Pāñcāla measure is common to all. Beyond this:
the Avanti measure is for Brahmins, and the Gāndhāra for a Kṣatriya;

1.56.s:
kaujanyamānaṃ vaiśyānāṃ viprādīnāṃ yathottaram /
yathoditaṃ jalastrāvyaṃ dvitribhūmikaveśmanām //
1.56.d:
कौजन्यमानं वैश्यानां विप्रादीनां यथोत्तरम् ।
यथोदितं जलस्त्राव्यं द्वित्रिभूमिकवेश्मनाम् ॥
1.56.m:
the Kaujanya measure is for Vaiśyas, and for Brahmins and the others in upward order.
As prescribed, water is to be drained from houses of two or three storeys.

1.56.s:
uṣṭrakuñjaraśālānāṃ dhvajāyepyathā vā gaje /
paśuśālāśca śālānāṃ dhvajāyepyatha vā gaje //
1.56.d:
उष्ट्रकुञ्जरशालानां ध्वजायेप्यथा वा गजे ।
पशुशालाश्च शालानां ध्वजायेप्यथ वा गजे ॥
1.56.m:
For stables of camels and elephants, [it should be] in the Dhvaja āya or else in the Gaja [āya];
and animal pens and halls, in the Dhvaja āya or else in the Gaja [āya].

1.56.s:
dvāraśayyāśanāmatradhvajāḥ siṃhavṛṣadhvajāḥ /
vāstupūjāvidhiṃ vakṣye navaveśmapraveśane //
1.56.d:
द्वारशय्याशनामत्रध्वजाः सिंहवृषध्वजाः ।
वास्तुपूजाविधिं वक्ष्ये नववेश्मप्रवेशने ॥
1.56.m:
For doors, beds, eating, and vessels: the Dhvaja, Siṃha, and Vṛṣa āyas.
I shall declare the ritual of worshipping the site upon entering a new dwelling.

1.56.s:
hastamātrā likhedrekhā daśa pūrvā daśottarāḥ /
gṛhamadhye taṇḍuloparyekāśītipadaṃ bhavet //
1.56.d:
हस्तमात्रा लिखेद्रेखा दश पूर्वा दशोत्तराः ।
गृहमध्ये तण्डुलोपर्येकाशीतिपदं भवेत् ॥
1.56.m:
One should draw ten lines to the east and ten to the north, measuring a cubit,
in the centre of the house upon raw rice; there shall be eighty-one squares.

1.56.s:
pañcottarānvakṣyamāṇāṃścatvariṃśatsurān likhet /
dvātrindvāhyataḥ pūjyāstatrāntaḥsthāsrayodaśa //
1.56.d:
पञ्चोत्तरान्वक्ष्यमाणांश्चत्वरिंशत्सुरान् लिखेत् ।
द्वात्रिन्द्वाह्यतः पूज्यास्तत्रान्तःस्थास्रयोदश ॥
1.56.m:
One should draw forty-five gods who will be spoken of:
thirty-two are to be worshipped on the outside, and thirteen residing within.

1.56.s:
teṣāṃ sthānāni nāmāni vakṣyāmi kramaśodhunā /
īśānakoṇato bāhyo dvātriṃśatrridaśā amī //
1.56.d:
तेषां स्थानानि नामानि वक्ष्यामि क्रमशोधुना ।
ईशानकोणतो बाह्यो द्वात्रिंशत्र्रिदशा अमी ॥
1.56.m:
I shall now declare their places and names in order:
from the north-east corner, on the outside, are these thirty-two gods:

1.56.s:
kṛpīṭayoniḥ parjanyo jayantaḥ pākaśāsanaḥ /
sūryaḥ śaśī mṛgākāśau vāyuḥ pūṣā ca nairṛtiḥ //
1.56.d:
कृपीटयोनिः पर्जन्यो जयन्तः पाकशासनः ।
सूर्यः शशी मृगाकाशौ वायुः पूषा च नैरृतिः ॥
1.56.m:
Kṛpīṭayoni, Parjanya, Jayanta, Pākaśāsana,
Sūrya, Śaśin, Mṛga, Ākāśa, Vāyu, Pūṣan, and Nairṛti,

1.56.s:
gṛhākṣato daṇḍadharo gāndharvo bhṛgurājakaḥ /
mṛgaḥ pitṛgaṇādhiśastato dauvāri kāhvayaḥ //
1.56.d:
गृहाक्षतो दण्डधरो गान्धर्वो भृगुराजकः ।
मृगः पितृगणाधिशस्ततो दौवारि काह्वयः ॥
1.56.m:
Gṛhākṣata, Daṇḍadhara, Gāndharva, Bhṛgurājaka,
Mṛga, the lord of the ancestral hosts, then the one named Dauvārika,

1.56.s:
sāmaḥ sūryo 'ditiditī dvātriṃśatrridaśā amī /
atheśānādikoṇasthāścātvārastatsamīpagāḥ //
1.56.d:
सामः सूर्यो ऽदितिदिती द्वात्रिंशत्र्रिदशा अमी ।
अथेशानादिकोणस्थाश्चात्वारस्तत्समीपगाः ॥
1.56.m:
Soma, Sūrya, Aditi, and Diti—these are the thirty-two gods.
Now the four situated in the corners beginning with the north-east, standing near them:

1.56.s:
āpaḥ sāvitraghasaṃjñaśca jayo rudraḥ kramādamī /
ekāntarā syuḥ prāgādyāḥ parito brahmaṇaḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.56.d:
आपः सावित्रघसंज्ञश्च जयो रुद्रः क्रमादमी ।
एकान्तरा स्युः प्रागाद्याः परितो ब्रह्मणः स्मृताः ॥
1.56.m:
Āpas, the one named Sāvitra, Jaya, and Rudra in due order.
Surrounding Brahmā, beginning with the east, are remembered [those with] one intervening space:

1.56.s:
aryamā savitā biṃbavivattkānvaktudhādhipaḥ /
mitrotha rājayakṣmā ca tathā pṛthvīdharāhvayaḥ //
1.56.d:
अर्यमा सविता बिंबविवत्त्कान्वक्तुधाधिपः ।
मित्रोथ राजयक्ष्मा च तथा पृथ्वीधराह्वयः ॥
1.56.m:
Aryaman, Savitṛ, Vivasvat, the lord of nectar [Vibhuda],
Mitra, then Rājayakṣman, and likewise the one named Pṛthvīdhara,

1.56.s:
āpavatso 'ṣṭamaḥ pañcacatvāriṃśatsurā amī /
āpaścaivāpavatsaśca parjanyo 'gnirditiḥ kramāt //
1.56.d:
आपवत्सो ऽष्टमः पञ्चचत्वारिंशत्सुरा अमी ।
आपश्चैवापवत्सश्च पर्जन्यो ऽग्निर्दितिः क्रमात् ॥
1.56.m:
and Āpavatsa as the eighth—these are the forty-five gods.
Āpas, Āpavatsa, Parjanya, Agni, and Diti, in order,

1.56.s:
yaddikkānāṃ ca vargo 'yamevaṃ koṇeṣvaśeṣataḥ /
tanmadhye viṃśatirbāhyā dvipadāste tu sarvadā //
1.56.d:
यद्दिक्कानां च वर्गो ऽयमेवं कोणेष्वशेषतः ।
तन्मध्ये विंशतिर्बाह्या द्विपदास्ते तु सर्वदा ॥
1.56.m:
and this group belonging to that direction—thus in all the corners.
Among them, the outer twenty always occupy two squares.

1.56.s:
aryamā ca vivasvāṃśca mitraḥ pṛthvī dharāhvayaḥ /
brahmaṇaḥ pārito dikṣu catvārastripadāḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.56.d:
अर्यमा च विवस्वांश्च मित्रः पृथ्वी धराह्वयः ।
ब्रह्मणः पारितो दिक्षु चत्वारस्त्रिपदाः स्मृताः ॥
1.56.m:
Aryaman, Vivasvat, Mitra, and the one named Pṛthvīdhara:
these four around Brahmā in the cardinal directions are remembered as occupying three squares.

1.56.s:
brahmāṇaṃ ca tathaikadvitripadānarcayetsurān /
vāstumantreṇa vāstujño dūrvādadhyakṣatādibhiḥ //
1.56.d:
ब्रह्माणं च तथैकद्वित्रिपदानर्चयेत्सुरान् ।
वास्तुमन्त्रेण वास्तुज्ञो दूर्वादध्यक्षतादिभिः ॥
1.56.m:
One who knows the site should worship Brahmā and likewise the gods occupying one, two, or three squares
with the Vāstu mantra, using dūrvā grass, curd, unbroken grains, and so forth,

1.56.s:
brahmamantreṇa vā śvetavastrayugmaṃ pradāpayet /
āvāhanādisarvopacārāṃśca kramaśastathā //
1.56.d:
ब्रह्ममन्त्रेण वा श्वेतवस्त्रयुग्मं प्रदापयेत् ।
आवाहनादिसर्वोपचारांश्च क्रमशस्तथा ॥
1.56.m:
or with the Brahmā mantra; one should present a pair of white cloths,
and likewise all the services in order, beginning with invocation.

1.56.s:
naivedyaṃ trividhānnena vādyaiḥ sahasamarpayet /
tāmbūlaṃ ca tataḥ kartā prārthayedvāstupūruṣam //
vāstupuruṣa namaste 'stu bhūśayyānirata prabho //
1.56.d:
नैवेद्यं त्रिविधान्नेन वाद्यैः सहसमर्पयेत् ।
ताम्बूलं च ततः कर्ता प्रार्थयेद्वास्तुपूरुषम् ॥
वास्तुपुरुष नमस्ते ऽस्तु भूशय्यानिरत प्रभो ॥
1.56.m:
He should present the food offering with three kinds of food along with musical instruments,
and betel; then the patron should pray to the site-man:

"O site-man, obeisance be to you, O Lord engaged in lying upon the earth!

1.56.s: madgṛhe dhanadhānyādisamṛddhaṃ kuru sarvadā //
1.56.d: मद्गृहे धनधान्यादिसमृद्धं कुरु सर्वदा ॥
1.56.m: "Make [my life] in my house always abundant with wealth, grain, and the like!"

1.56.s:
iti prārthya yathāśaktyā dakṣiṇāmarcakāya ca /
dadyāttadagre viprebhyo bhojanaṃ ca svaśaktitaḥ //
1.56.d:
इति प्रार्थ्य यथाशक्त्या दक्षिणामर्चकाय च ।
दद्यात्तदग्रे विप्रेभ्यो भोजनं च स्वशक्तितः ॥
1.56.m: Having prayed thus, one should give a sacrificial fee according to one's means to the worshipper, / and in front of him one should give food to the brāhmaṇas according to one's capacity.

1.56.s:
anena vidhinā samyagvāstupūjāṃ karoti yaḥ /
ārogyaṃ putralābhaṃ ca dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ labhennaraḥ //
1.56.d:
अनेन विधिना सम्यग्वास्तुपूजां करोति यः ।
आरोग्यं पुत्रलाभं च धनं धान्यं लभेन्नरः ॥
1.56.m: The man who duly performs the worship of the Vāstu deity according to this rule / obtains health, the birth of sons, wealth, and grain.

1.56.s:
akṛtvā vāstupūjāṃ yaḥ praviśennavamandiram /
rogānnānāvidhānkleśānaśnute sarvasaṃkaṭam //
1.56.d:
अकृत्वा वास्तुपूजां यः प्रविशेन्नवमन्दिरम् ।
रोगान्नानाविधान्क्लेशानश्नुते सर्वसंकटम् ॥
1.56.m: He who enters a new house without having performed the Vāstu worship / suffers from diseases, various kinds of afflictions, and all manner of distress.

1.56.s:
akapāṭamanācchannamadattabalibhojanam /
gṛhaṃ na praviśedevaṃ vipadāmākaraṃ hi tat //
1.56.d:
अकपाटमनाच्छन्नमदत्तबलिभोजनम् ।
गृहं न प्रविशेदेवं विपदामाकरं हि तत् ॥
1.56.m: One must never enter a house that has no doors, is uncovered, / and in which offerings and food have not been given; for it is a mine of calamities.

1.56.s:
atho yātrā nṛpādīnāmabhīṣṭaphalasiddhaye /
syāttathā tāṃ pravakṣyāmi samyagvijñātajanmanām //
1.56.d:
अथो यात्रा नृपादीनामभीष्टफलसिद्धये ।
स्यात्तथा तां प्रवक्ष्यामि सम्यग्विज्ञातजन्मनाम् ॥
1.56.m: Now, for kings and others whose birth[-times] are well known, / I shall explain journeying so that it leads to the attainment of the desired results.

1.56.s:
ajñātajanmanāṃ nṝṇāṃ phalāptirghuṇavarṇavat /
praśnodayanimittādyaisteṣāmapi phalodayaḥ //
1.56.d:
अज्ञातजन्मनां नॄणां फलाप्तिर्घुणवर्णवत् ।
प्रश्नोदयनिमित्ताद्यैस्तेषामपि फलोदयः ॥
1.56.m: For men whose birth[-times] are unknown, the attainment of results is like letters bored by a woodworm; / their attainment of results also arises from queries, the rising sign, omens, and the like.

1.56.s:
ṣaṣṭyaṣṭamīdvādaśīṣu riktāmāpūrṇimāsu ca /
yātrā śuklapratipadi nirddhanāya kṣayāya ca //
1.56.d:
षष्ट्यष्टमीद्वादशीषु रिक्तामापूर्णिमासु च ।
यात्रा शुक्लप्रतिपदि निर्द्धनाय क्षयाय च ॥
1.56.m: On the sixth, eighth, and twelfth [lunar days], on the empty lunar days, the new moon, and the full moon, / and on the first lunar day of the bright fortnight, a journey leads to poverty and ruin.

1.56.s:
maitrāditīndvārkāntyāśvihāgitiṣyavasūḍuṣu /
asaptapañcatryādyeṣu yātrābhīṣṭaphalapradāḥ //
1.56.d:
मैत्रादितीन्द्वार्कान्त्याश्विहागितिष्यवसूडुषु ।
असप्तपञ्चत्र्याद्येषु यात्राभीष्टफलप्रदाः ॥
1.56.m: In the asterisms of Anurādhā, Punarvasu, Mṛgaśīrṣa, Hasta, Revatī, Aśvinī, Puṣya, and Dhaniṣṭhā, / when they are not the seventh, fifth, or third [from one's birth-star] or the first, journeys grant desired results.

1.56.s:
na mandendudine prācīṃ na vrajeddakṣiṇaṃ gurau /
sitārkayerna pratīcīṃ nodīcīṃ jñārayorddine //
1.56.d:
न मन्देन्दुदिने प्राचीं न व्रजेद्दक्षिणं गुरौ ।
सितार्कयेर्न प्रतीचीं नोदीचीं ज्ञारयोर्द्दिने ॥
1.56.m: One should not travel east on the day of Saturn or the Moon, nor south on Jupiter's day; / nor west on the day of Venus or the Sun, nor north on the day of Mercury or Mars.

1.56.s:
indrājapādacaturāsyāryamarkṣāṇi pūrvataḥ /
śūlāni sarvadvārāṇi mitrārkejyāśvabhāni ca //
1.56.d:
इन्द्राजपादचतुरास्यार्यमर्क्षाणि पूर्वतः ।
शूलानि सर्वद्वाराणि मित्रार्केज्याश्वभानि च ॥
1.56.m: The asterisms of Jyeṣṭhā, Pūrvabhādrapadā, Rohiṇī, and Uttarāphālgunī are [directional] spikes in the east; / and all gates are [reckoned with] the asterisms of Anurādhā, Hasta, Puṣya, and Aśvinī.

1.56.s:
kramāddigdvārabhāni syuḥ saptasaptāgnidhiṣṇyataḥ /
parighaṃ laṅghayeddaṇḍaṃ nāgniśvasanardiggamam //
1.56.d:
क्रमाद्दिग्द्वारभानि स्युः सप्तसप्ताग्निधिष्ण्यतः ।
परिघं लङ्घयेद्दण्डं नाग्निश्वसनर्दिग्गमम् ॥
1.56.m: In order, seven asterisms from the asterism of Kṛttikā become the gate-stars of the quarters. / One may cross the bar and the rod, but one must not travel toward the quarters of fire and wind.

1.56.s:
āgneyaṃ pūrvadigdhiṣṇyairvidiśaścaivameva hi /
digrāśayastu kramaśo meṣādyāśca punaḥ punaḥ //
1.56.d:
आग्नेयं पूर्वदिग्धिष्ण्यैर्विदिशश्चैवमेव हि ।
दिग्राशयस्तु क्रमशो मेषाद्याश्च पुनः पुनः ॥
1.56.m: The south-east is reckoned by the stars of the eastern direction, and likewise the intermediate directions; / and the directional zodiacal signs are repeatedly Aries and the others in order.

1.56.s:
digīśvare lalāṭasthe yāturna punarāgamaḥ /
lagnastho bhāskaraḥ prācyāṃ diśi yāturlalāṭagaḥ //
1.56.d:
दिगीश्वरे ललाटस्थे यातुर्न पुनरागमः ।
लग्नस्थो भास्करः प्राच्यां दिशि यातुर्ललाटगः ॥
1.56.m: When the lord of a direction stands on the traveler's forehead, he does not return. / The Sun situated in the ascendant stands on the forehead of one travelling in the eastern direction.

1.56.s:
dvādaśaikādaśaḥ śukro 'pyāgneyyāntu lalāṭagaḥ /
daśamasthaḥ kujo lagnādyābhyāṃ yāturlalāṭagaḥ //
1.56.d:
द्वादशैकादशः शुक्रो ऽप्याग्नेय्यान्तु ललाटगः ।
दशमस्थः कुजो लग्नाद्याभ्यां यातुर्ललाटगः ॥
1.56.m: Venus in the twelfth or eleventh stands on the forehead in the south-east; / Mars situated in the tenth from the ascendant stands on the forehead of a traveler heading south.

1.56.s:
navamāṣṭamago rāhurnaiṛtyāṃ tu lalāṭagaḥ /
lagnātsaptamagaḥ sauriḥ pratīcyāṃ tu lalāṭagaḥ //
1.56.d:
नवमाष्टमगो राहुर्नैऋत्यां तु ललाटगः ।
लग्नात्सप्तमगः सौरिः प्रतीच्यां तु ललाटगः ॥
1.56.m: Rāhu in the ninth or eighth stands on the forehead in the south-west; / Saturn in the seventh from the ascendant stands on the forehead in the west.

1.56.s:
ṣaṣṭaḥ pañcamagaścandro vāyavyāṃ ca lalāṭagaḥ /
caturthasthānagaḥ saumyaścottarasyāṃ lalāṭagaḥ //
1.56.d:
षष्टः पञ्चमगश्चन्द्रो वायव्यां च ललाटगः ।
चतुर्थस्थानगः सौम्यश्चोत्तरस्यां ललाटगः ॥
1.56.m: The Moon in the sixth or fifth stands on the forehead in the north-west; / and Mercury situated in the fourth house stands on the forehead in the north.

1.56.s:
dvitristhānagato jīva īśānyāṃ vai lalāṭagaḥ /
lalāṭaṃ tu parityajya jīvitecchurvrajennaraḥ //
1.56.d:
द्वित्रिस्थानगतो जीव ईशान्यां वै ललाटगः ।
ललाटं तु परित्यज्य जीवितेच्छुर्व्रजेन्नरः ॥
1.56.m: Jupiter located in the second or third house stands on the forehead in the north-east. / A man wishing to live should depart avoiding [the planet on his] forehead.

1.56.s:
vilomago graho yasya yātrālagropago yadi /
tasya bhaṅgaprado rājñasta dvargo 'pi vilagnagaḥ //
1.56.d:
विलोमगो ग्रहो यस्य यात्रालग्रोपगो यदि ।
तस्य भङ्गप्रदो राज्ञस्त द्वर्गो ऽपि विलग्नगः ॥
1.56.m: If a planet moving retrograde is in the journey's rising sign of anyone, / it brings defeat to that king; and likewise if its division is in the ascendant.

1.56.s:
ravīndvayanayoryātamanukūlaṃ śubhapradam /
tadabhāve divārātrau yāyādyāturvadho 'nyathā //
1.56.d:
रवीन्द्वयनयोर्यातमनुकूलं शुभप्रदम् ।
तदभावे दिवारात्रौ यायाद्यातुर्वधो ऽन्यथा ॥
1.56.m: A departure favorable to the solstices of the Sun and the Moon brings good fortune; / in their absence, one should travel by day or night [respectively], otherwise the traveler suffers destruction.

1.56.s:
mūḍhe śukre kāryahāniḥ pratiśukre parājayaḥ /
pratiśukrakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ hṝntuṃ śaktā grahā na hi //
1.56.d:
मूढे शुक्रे कार्यहानिः प्रतिशुक्रे पराजयः ।
प्रतिशुक्रकृतं दोषं हॄन्तुं शक्ता ग्रहा न हि ॥
1.56.m: When Venus is combust, there is loss of the undertaking; when Venus is directly opposite, there is defeat; / the planets are not capable of removing the flaw caused by an opposing Venus.

1.56.s:
vāsiṣṭakāśyapeyātribhāradvājāḥ sagautamāḥ /
eteṣāṃ pañcagotrāṇāṃ pratiśukro na vidyate //
1.56.d:
वासिष्टकाश्यपेयात्रिभारद्वाजाः सगौतमाः ।
एतेषां पञ्चगोत्राणां प्रतिशुक्रो न विद्यते ॥
1.56.m: For the descendants of Vasiṣṭha, Kaśyapa, Atri, and Bharadvāja, along with those of Gautama— / for these five clans an opposing Venus does not exist.

1.56.s:
ekagrāme vivāhe ca durbhikṣe rājavigrahe /
dvijakṣobhe nṛpakṣobhe pratiśukro na vidyate //
1.56.d:
एकग्रामे विवाहे च दुर्भिक्षे राजविग्रहे ।
द्विजक्षोभे नृपक्षोभे प्रतिशुक्रो न विद्यते ॥
1.56.m: In the same village, in marriage, during famine, during a war between kings, / during distress caused by brāhmaṇas, or distress caused by kings, an opposing Venus does not exist.

1.56.s:
nīcago 'rigṛhastho vā vakrago vā parājitaḥ /
yāturbhaṅgapradaḥ śukraḥ svoñcasthaścejjayapradaḥ //
1.56.d:
नीचगो ऽरिगृहस्थो वा वक्रगो वा पराजितः ।
यातुर्भङ्गप्रदः शुक्रः स्वोञ्चस्थश्चेज्जयप्रदः ॥
1.56.m: When Venus is debilitated, in an enemy's house, retrograde, or defeated in planetary war, / it brings defeat to the traveler; but if situated in its exaltation, it brings victory.

1.56.s:
svāṣṭalagneṣṭarāśau vā śatrubhāttvaṣṭamepi vā /
teṣāmīśastharāśau vā yāturmṛtyurna saṃśayaḥ //
1.56.d:
स्वाष्टलग्नेष्टराशौ वा शत्रुभात्त्वष्टमेपि वा ।
तेषामीशस्थराशौ वा यातुर्मृत्युर्न संशयः ॥
1.56.m: If [the journey's ascendant] is in one's eighth sign from the ascendant, or the eighth sign from the enemy's star, / or in the sign occupied by their lords, the traveler's death is beyond doubt.

1.56.s:
janmeṣāṣṭamalagneśau mitho mitre vyavasthitau /
janmarāśyaṣṭamarkṣotthadoṣā naśyantiṃ bhāktaḥ //
1.56.d:
जन्मेषाष्टमलग्नेशौ मिथो मित्रे व्यवस्थितौ ।
जन्मराश्यष्टमर्क्षोत्थदोषा नश्यन्तिं भाक्तः ॥
1.56.m: If the lord of the birth sign and the lord of the eighth or the ascendant are situated as mutual friends, / the flaws arising from the eighth star from the birth sign are eliminated in turn.

1.56.s:
krūragrahekṣito yukto dviḥsvabhāvo 'pi bhaṅgadaḥ /
yāne sthirodaye neṣṭo bhavyayuktekṣitaḥ svayam //
1.56.d:
क्रूरग्रहेक्षितो युक्तो द्विःस्वभावो ऽपि भङ्गदः ।
याने स्थिरोदये नेष्टो भव्ययुक्तेक्षितः स्वयम् ॥
1.56.m: Even a dual sign aspected by or conjoined with a malefic planet brings failure; / on a journey, a fixed sign rising is not desired, even if it is conjoined with or aspected by a benefic.

1.56.s:
vasvantyārddhādipañcarkṣe saṃgrahaṃ tṛṇakāṣṭayoḥ /
yāmyadiggamanaṃ śayyā na kuryādgehagopanam //
1.56.d:
वस्वन्त्यार्द्धादिपञ्चर्क्षे संग्रहं तृणकाष्टयोः ।
याम्यदिग्गमनं शय्या न कुर्याद्गेहगोपनम् ॥
1.56.m: In the five asterisms beginning with the second half of Dhaniṣṭhā, / one should not make a gathering of grass and wood, travel to the south, make a bed, or thatch a house.

1.56.s:
janmodaye janmabhe vā tayorīśasyabhepi vā /
tābhyāṃ tayorikendreṣu yātuḥ śatrukṣayo bhavet //
1.56.d:
जन्मोदये जन्मभे वा तयोरीशस्यभेपि वा ।
ताभ्यां तयोरिकेन्द्रेषु यातुः शत्रुक्षयो भवेत् ॥
1.56.m: When the birth-ascendant, the birth-star, or the star of their lords rises, / or when in the angles from those two [benefics are placed], the traveler accomplishes the destruction of the enemy.

1.56.s:
śīrṣodaye lagnagate diglagne lagnagopi vā /
śubhavārgotha vā lagne yātuḥ śatrukṣayastadā //
1.56.d:
शीर्षोदये लग्नगते दिग्लग्ने लग्नगोपि वा ।
शुभवार्गोथ वा लग्ने यातुः शत्रुक्षयस्तदा ॥
1.56.m: When a sign that rises head-first is in the ascendant, or a directional sign is in the ascendant, / or a benefic division is in the ascendant, then destruction of the enemy belongs to the traveler.

1.56.s:
śatrujanmodaye janmarāśervā nidhanodaye /
tayorīśasthite rāśau yātuḥ śatrukṣayo bhavet //
1.56.d:
शत्रुजन्मोदये जन्मराशेर्वा निधनोदये ।
तयोरीशस्थिते राशौ यातुः शत्रुक्षयो भवेत् ॥
1.56.m: When the enemy's birth-ascendant or the eighth sign from his birth-sign rises, / or in the sign occupied by their lords, destruction of the enemy belongs to the traveler.

1.56.s:
vakraḥ panthā mīnalagne yāturmīnāṃśakepi vā /
nindyo nikhilayātrāsu ghaṭalagno ghaṭāṃśakaḥ //
1.56.d:
वक्रः पन्था मीनलग्ने यातुर्मीनांशकेपि वा ।
निन्द्यो निखिलयात्रासु घटलग्नो घटांशकः ॥
1.56.m: The path is crooked when Pisces is the rising sign or in a navāṃśa of Pisces for the traveler; / Aquarius as the rising sign or a navāṃśa of Aquarius is condemned in all journeys.

1.56.s:
jalalagno jalāṃśo vā jalayoneḥ śubhāvahaḥ /
mūrtiḥ kośo dhanvinaśca vāhanaṃ mantrasaṃjñakam //
1.56.d:
जललग्नो जलांशो वा जलयोनेः शुभावहः ।
मूर्तिः कोशो धन्विनश्च वाहनं मन्त्रसंज्ञकम् ॥
1.56.m: A water-sign or water-division brings good fortune to one born of water. / The body, treasury, archers, conveyance, that named counsel,

1.56.s:
śatrumārgastathāyuśca manovyāpārasaṃjñikam /
prāptiraprāptirudayādbhāvāḥ syurdvādaśaiva te //
1.56.d:
शत्रुमार्गस्तथायुश्च मनोव्यापारसंज्ञिकम् ।
प्राप्तिरप्राप्तिरुदयाद्भावाः स्युर्द्वादशैव ते ॥
1.56.m: the enemy's path, longevity, that named mental activity, / gain, and non-gain—these are the twelve houses from the ascendant.

1.56.s:
ghnanti krūrāstryāptivargaṃ bhāvānsūryamahīsutau /
na nighnato hi vyāpāraṃ saumyāḥḍha puṣṇantyariṃ vinā //
1.56.d:
घ्नन्ति क्रूरास्त्र्याप्तिवर्गं भावान्सूर्यमहीसुतौ ।
न निघ्नतो हि व्यापारं सौम्याःढ पुष्णन्त्यरिं विना ॥
1.56.m: The malefics destroy the third and eleventh houses; the Sun and Mars / do not destroy action; benefics nurture [all houses] except the enemy house.

1.56.s:
śukro 'staṃ ca na puṣṇāti mūrtiṃ mṛtyuṃ ca candramāḥ /
yāmyadiggamanaṃ tyaktvā sarvakāṣṭhāsu yāyinām //
1.56.d:
शुक्रो ऽस्तं च न पुष्णाति मूर्तिं मृत्युं च चन्द्रमाः ।
याम्यदिग्गमनं त्यक्त्वा सर्वकाष्ठासु यायिनाम् ॥
1.56.m: Venus does not nurture the seventh house, nor the Moon the first and eighth houses. / For those travelling in all quarters, excluding travel in the southern direction,

1.56.s:
abhijitkṣaṇayogo 'yamabhīṣṭaphalasiddhidaḥ /
pañcāṅgaśuddhirahite divase 'pi phalapradaḥ //
1.56.d:
अभिजित्क्षणयोगो ऽयमभीष्टफलसिद्धिदः ।
पञ्चाङ्गशुद्धिरहिते दिवसे ऽपि फलप्रदः ॥
1.56.m: this planetary combination at the moment of Abhijit grants the attainment of desired results; / it bestows results even on a day devoid of purity of the five astrological limbs.

1.56.s:
yātrāyogā vicitrāstānyogānvakṣye yatastataḥ /
phalasiddhiryāgalagnādrājñāṃ vipraśya dhiṣṇyataḥ //
1.56.d:
यात्रायोगा विचित्रास्तान्योगान्वक्ष्ये यतस्ततः ।
फलसिद्धिर्यागलग्नाद्राज्ञां विप्रश्य धिष्ण्यतः ॥
1.56.m: Diverse are the combinations for travel; I shall describe those combinations from which / attainment of results occurs: for kings from the ascendant of sacrifice, for a brāhmaṇa from the star,

1.56.s:
muhūrtaśaktito 'nyeṣāṃ śakunaistaskarasya ca /
kendratrikoṇe hyekena yogaḥ śukrajñasūriṇām //
1.56.d:
मुहूर्तशक्तितो ऽन्येषां शकुनैस्तस्करस्य च ।
केन्द्रत्रिकोणे ह्येकेन योगः शुक्रज्ञसूरिणाम् ॥
1.56.m: for others from the power of the muhūrta, and for a thief from omens. / When one of Venus, Mercury, and Jupiter is in an angle or trine, a yoga is formed;

1.56.s:
adhiyego bhaveddvābhyāṃ tribhiryogādhiyogakaḥ /
yoge 'pi yāyināṃ kṣemamadhiyoge jayo bhavet //
1.56.d:
अधियेगो भवेद्द्वाभ्यां त्रिभिर्योगाधियोगकः ।
योगे ऽपि यायिनां क्षेममधियोगे जयो भवेत् ॥
1.56.m: with two of them it becomes an adhiyoga; with three it becomes a yogādhiyoga. / Even in a yoga there is security for travelers; in an adhiyoga there is victory;

1.56.s:
yogādhiyoge kṣemaṃ ca vijayārthavibhūtayaḥ /
