vyāpāraśatrumūrtisthaiścandramandadivākaraiḥ //
1.56.d:
योगाधियोगे क्षेमं च विजयार्थविभूतयः ।
व्यापारशत्रुमूर्तिस्थैश्चन्द्रमन्ददिवाकरैः ॥
1.56.m: and in a yogādhiyoga there is security, victory, wealth, and power. / When the Moon, Saturn, and the Sun are situated respectively in the tenth, sixth, and first houses,

1.56.s:
raṇe gatasya bhūpasya jayalakṣmīḥ pramāṇikā /
śukrārkajñārkibhaumeṣu lagnādhvastatriśatruṣu //
1.56.d:
रणे गतस्य भूपस्य जयलक्ष्मीः प्रमाणिका ।
शुक्रार्कज्ञार्किभौमेषु लग्नाध्वस्तत्रिशत्रुषु ॥
1.56.m: the fortune of victory is certain for a king who has gone to battle. / When Venus, the Sun, Mercury, Saturn, and Mars are situated in the ascendant, seventh, third, and sixth houses,

1.56.s:
gatasyāgre vairicamṛrvahnau lākṣve līyate /
lagnasthe tridaśācārye dhanāyasthaiḥ paragrahaiḥ //
1.56.d:
गतस्याग्रे वैरिचमृर्वह्नौ लाक्ष्वे लीयते ।
लग्नस्थे त्रिदशाचार्ये धनायस्थैः परग्रहैः ॥
1.56.m: the army of the enemy melts away like lac in fire before him who has marched forth. / When the preceptor of the thirty gods is in the ascendant, and the other planets are in the second and eleventh,

1.56.s:
gatasya rājño 'risenā nīyate yamamandiram /
lagne śukre ravau lābhe candre bandhusthite yadā //
1.56.d:
गतस्य राज्ञो ऽरिसेना नीयते यममन्दिरम् ।
लग्ने शुक्रे रवौ लाभे चन्द्रे बन्धुस्थिते यदा ॥
1.56.m: the enemy's army of the departed king is led to the abode of Yama. / When Venus is in the ascendant, the Sun in the eleventh, and the Moon is situated in the fourth house,

1.56.s:
gato nṛpo ripūnhṝnti kesarīvebhasaṃhatim /
svoccasaṃsthe site lagne svocce candre ca lābhage //
1.56.d:
गतो नृपो रिपून्हॄन्ति केसरीवेभसंहतिम् ।
स्वोच्चसंस्थे सिते लग्ने स्वोच्चे चन्द्रे च लाभगे ॥
1.56.m: The king who has marched slays his foes like a lion destroys a herd of elephants, / when Venus is in its exaltation in the ascendant, and the Moon is in its exaltation and situated in the eleventh house.

1.56.s:
hṝnti yāto 'riṣṭatanāṃ keśavaḥpūtanāmiva /
trikoṇe kendragāḥ saumyāḥ krūrāstryāyārigā yadi //
1.56.d:
हॄन्ति यातो ऽरिष्टतनां केशवःपूतनामिव ।
त्रिकोणे केन्द्रगाः सौम्याः क्रूरास्त्र्यायारिगा यदि ॥
1.56.m: Departing, he slays the enemy's army just as Keśava slew Pūtanā, / if the benefic planets are in trines and angles, and the malefic planets are in the third, eleventh, and sixth houses.

1.56.s:
yasya yāteralakṣmīstamupaitīvābhisārikā /
jīvārkacandrā lagnārirandhragā yadi gacchataḥ //
1.56.d:
यस्य यातेरलक्ष्मीस्तमुपैतीवाभिसारिका ।
जीवार्कचन्द्रा लग्नारिरन्ध्रगा यदि गच्छतः ॥
1.56.m: Misfortune approaches the traveler like a courting mistress, / if Jupiter, the Sun, and the Moon occupy the ascendant, sixth, and eighth houses for one who is marching.

1.56.s:
tasyāgre khalamaitrīva na sthirā ripuvāhinī /
trikhaḍāyeṣu mandārau balavantaḥ śubhā yadi //
1.56.d:
तस्याग्रे खलमैत्रीव न स्थिरा रिपुवाहिनी ।
त्रिखडायेषु मन्दारौ बलवन्तः शुभा यदि ॥
1.56.m: Before him, the enemy army is unstable like the friendship of a rogue, / if Saturn and Mars are in the third, sixth, and eleventh houses, and the benefics are strong.

1.56.s:
yātrāyāṃ nṛpatastasya hastasthā śatrumedinī /
svoñcasthe lagnage jīve candre lābhagate yadi //
1.56.d:
यात्रायां नृपतस्तस्य हस्तस्था शत्रुमेदिनी ।
स्वोञ्चस्थे लग्नगे जीवे चन्द्रे लाभगते यदि ॥
1.56.m: Upon the expedition of that king, the enemy’s territory falls into his hand, / if Jupiter is in the ascendant in its exaltation, and the Moon is in the eleventh house.

1.56.s:
gato rājā ripūnhati pinākī tripuraṃ yathā /
mastakodayageśukra lagnasthe lābhage gurau //
1.56.d:
गतो राजा रिपून्हति पिनाकी त्रिपुरं यथा ।
मस्तकोदयगेशुक्र लग्नस्थे लाभगे गुरौ ॥
1.56.m: The king who has marched slays his enemies just as Pinākin destroyed Tripura, / when Venus rises head-first in the ascendant, and Jupiter is in the eleventh house.

1.56.s:
gato rājā ripūnhṝnti kumārastārakaṃ yathā /
jīvaṃ lagnagate śukre kendre vāpi trikoṇage //
1.56.d:
गतो राजा रिपून्हॄन्ति कुमारस्तारकं यथा ।
जीवं लग्नगते शुक्रे केन्द्रे वापि त्रिकोणगे ॥
1.56.m: The king who has marched slays his enemies just as Kumāra slew Tāraka, / when Jupiter is in the ascendant and Venus is in an angle or in a trine.

1.56.s:
gato dahatyarīvrājā kṛṣṇavartmā yathā vanam /
lagnage jñe śubhe kendre dhiṣṇye copakule gataḥ //
1.56.d:
गतो दहत्यरीव्राजा कृष्णवर्त्मा यथा वनम् ।
लग्नगे ज्ञे शुभे केन्द्रे धिष्ण्ये चोपकुले गतः ॥
1.56.m: The king who has marched burns his enemies like fire burns a forest, / when Mercury is in the ascendant and a benefic is in an angle, and the departure takes place under a favorable asterism and allied constellation.

1.56.s:
nṛpāḥ śuṣyantyarīn grīṣme hradinīṃ vārkaraśmayaḥ /
śubhi trikoṇe kendrasthe lābhe candre 'thavā ravī //
1.56.d:
नृपाः शुष्यन्त्यरीन् ग्रीष्मे ह्रदिनीं वार्करश्मयः ।
शुभि त्रिकोणे केन्द्रस्थे लाभे चन्द्रे ऽथवा रवी ॥
1.56.m: Kings dry up their enemies like the rays of the sun dry up a pond in summer, / when a benefic is in a trine or angle, and the Moon or the Sun is in the eleventh house.

1.56.s:
śatrūnhanti gato rājā hyandhakāraṃ yathā raviḥ /
svakṣetrage śubhe kadre trikoṇoyagate gataḥ //
1.56.d:
शत्रून्हन्ति गतो राजा ह्यन्धकारं यथा रविः ।
स्वक्षेत्रगे शुभे कद्रे त्रिकोणोयगते गतः ॥
1.56.m: The king who has marched slays his enemies just as the sun dispels darkness, / when a benefic is in its own house and in an angle, and the departure takes place with a planet in a trine.

1.56.s:
vināśayatyarītrājā tṛlarāśimivānalaḥ /
indau svasthe gurau kendre mantraḥ sapraṇavo gataḥ //
1.56.d:
विनाशयत्यरीत्राजा तृलराशिमिवानलः ।
इन्दौ स्वस्थे गुरौ केन्द्रे मन्त्रः सप्रणवो गतः ॥
1.56.m: The king destroys his enemies like fire destroys a heap of grass; / the departure is like a mantra with the praṇava, when the Moon is in its own house and Jupiter is in an angle.

1.56.s:
nṝpo hṝnti ripūnsarvānpāpānpañcākṣaro yathā /
vargottamagate śukre 'pyevasminneva lagnage //
1.56.d:
नॄपो हॄन्ति रिपून्सर्वान्पापान्पञ्चाक्षरो यथा ।
वर्गोत्तमगते शुक्रे ऽप्येवस्मिन्नेव लग्नगे ॥
1.56.m: The king slays all his enemies just as the five-syllable mantra destroys sins, / when Venus is in the vargottama division and in that very ascendant.

1.56.s:
harismṛtiryathāghaughānhṝnti śatrūn gato nṛpaḥ /
śubhe kendre trikoṇasthe candre vargottame gataḥ //
1.56.d:
हरिस्मृतिर्यथाघौघान्हॄन्ति शत्रून् गतो नृपः ।
शुभे केन्द्रे त्रिकोणस्थे चन्द्रे वर्गोत्तमे गतः ॥
1.56.m: Just as the remembrance of Hari destroys floods of sins, the king who has marched slays his enemies, / when a benefic is in an angle or a trine, and the departure occurs with the Moon in vargottama.

1.56.s:
sagotrārīnnṛpān hṝnti yathā gotrāṃścagotrabhit /
mitrabhe 'tha gurau kendre trikoṇasthe 'tha vā site //
1.56.d:
सगोत्रारीन्नृपान् हॄन्ति यथा गोत्रांश्चगोत्रभित् ।
मित्रभे ऽथ गुरौ केन्द्रे त्रिकोणस्थे ऽथ वा सिते ॥
1.56.m: He slays enemy kings of the same lineage just as the breaker of mountains [Indra] struck down the mountains, / when Jupiter is in a friendly sign and in an angle, or when Venus is in a trine.

1.56.s:
śatrūnhṝnti gato rājā bhujaṅgān garuḍo yathā /
śubhakadratrikoṇasthe vargottamagate gataḥ //
1.56.d:
शत्रून्हॄन्ति गतो राजा भुजङ्गान् गरुडो यथा ।
शुभकद्रत्रिकोणस्थे वर्गोत्तमगते गतः ॥
1.56.m: The king who has marched slays his enemies just as Garuḍa slays serpents, / when the departure occurs with a benefic in an angle or a trine and in vargottama.

1.56.s:
vināśayatyarīnrājā pāpānbhāgīrathī yathā /
ye nṛpā yāntyarīñjetuṃ teṣāṃ yogairnṛpāhvayaiḥ //
1.56.d:
विनाशयत्यरीन्राजा पापान्भागीरथी यथा ।
ये नृपा यान्त्यरीञ्जेतुं तेषां योगैर्नृपाह्वयैः ॥
1.56.m: The king destroys his enemies just as the Bhāgīrathī washes away sins. / For kings who march to conquer enemies under these astrological combinations named after kings,

1.56.s:
upaiti śāntiṃ kopāgniḥ śatruyoṣāśrubindubhiḥ /
balakṣayapakṣadaśamīmāsīṣe vijayābhidhā //
1.56.d:
उपैति शान्तिं कोपाग्निः शत्रुयोषाश्रुबिन्दुभिः ।
बलक्षयपक्षदशमीमासीषे विजयाभिधा ॥
1.56.m: the fire of anger is quenched by the teardrops of the enemy’s women. / On the tenth tithi of the waning fortnight in the month of Āśvina, which is named Vijayā,

1.56.s:
vijayastatra yātṝṇāṃ sadhirvā na parājayaḥ /
nimittaśakunādibhyaḥ pradhānaṃ hi manodayaḥ //
1.56.d:
विजयस्तत्र यातॄणां सधिर्वा न पराजयः ।
निमित्तशकुनादिभ्यः प्रधानं हि मनोदयः ॥
1.56.m: victory belongs to those who march, or an honorable peace, but not defeat. / Indeed, superior to omens, birds, and portents is the rising of inner resolve;

1.56.s:
tasmānmanasvināṃ yatnātphalaheturmanodayaḥ /
utsavopanayodvāhapratiṣṭāśaucasūtake //
1.56.d:
तस्मान्मनस्विनां यत्नात्फलहेतुर्मनोदयः ।
उत्सवोपनयोद्वाहप्रतिष्टाशौचसूतके ॥
1.56.m: therefore, for resolute men, the rising of resolve is deliberately the cause of success. / During a festival, an upanayana, a wedding, a consecration, or ritual impurity from death or birth,

1.56.s:
asamāpte na kurvīta yātrāṃ martyo jijīviṣuḥ /
mahiṣondurayoryuddhe kalatrakalahārttave //
1.56.d:
असमाप्ते न कुर्वीत यात्रां मर्त्यो जिजीविषुः ।
महिषोन्दुरयोर्युद्धे कलत्रकलहार्त्तवे ॥
1.56.m: a mortal desiring to live should not set out on an expedition before these are completed; / nor during a fight between a buffalo and a rat, a marital quarrel, or [the wife's] menses;

1.56.s:
vastrādeḥ skhalite krodhe durukte na vrajennṛpaḥ /
ghṛtānnaṃ tilapiṣṭānnaṃ matsyānnaṃ ghṛtapāyasam //
1.56.d:
वस्त्रादेः स्खलिते क्रोधे दुरुक्ते न व्रजेन्नृपः ।
घृतान्नं तिलपिष्टान्नं मत्स्यान्नं घृतपायसम् ॥
1.56.m: nor upon the slipping of a garment, during anger, or at harsh words should a king march. / Having eaten food cooked with ghee, food with sesame paste, fish with rice, or sweet rice-pudding with ghee,

1.56.s:
prāgādikramaśo bhuktvā yāti rājā jayatyarīn /
sajjikā paramānnaṃ ca kāñjika ca payo dadhi //
1.56.d:
प्रागादिक्रमशो भुक्त्वा याति राजा जयत्यरीन् ।
सज्जिका परमान्नं च काञ्जिक च पयो दधि ॥
1.56.m: in order starting from the east, the king marches and conquers his foes. / Having eaten barley gruel, divine rice-pudding, sour gruel, milk, curd,

1.56.s:
kṣīraṃ tilodanaṃ bhuktvā bhānuvārādiṣu kramāt /
kulmāṣāṃśca tilānnaṃ ca dadhi kṣaudraṃ ghṛtaṃ payaḥ //
1.56.d:
क्षीरं तिलोदनं भुक्त्वा भानुवारादिषु क्रमात् ।
कुल्माषांश्च तिलान्नं च दधि क्षौद्रं घृतं पयः ॥
1.56.m: condensed milk, and sesame-rice in sequence on Sunday and the other days of the week; / and sour gruel, sesame-rice, curd, honey, ghee, milk,

1.56.s:
mṛgamāṃsaṃ ca tatsāraṃ pāyasaṃ ca khagaṃ mṛgam /
śaśamāṃsaṃ ca ṣāṣṭikyaṃ priyaguṅkamapūpakam //
1.56.d:
मृगमांसं च तत्सारं पायसं च खगं मृगम् ।
शशमांसं च षाष्टिक्यं प्रियगुङ्कमपूपकम् ॥
1.56.m: venison and its broth, sweet rice-pudding, fowl, deer meat, / hare meat, ṣaṣṭika-rice, priyaṅgu-grain, cakes,

1.56.s:
citrāṇḍajapalaṃ kūrmaśvāvidgodhāṃśca śāsvakam /
haviṣyaṃ kṛśarānnaṃ ca mudgānnaṃ yavapiṣṭikam //
1.56.d:
चित्राण्डजपलं कूर्मश्वाविद्गोधांश्च शास्वकम् ।
हविष्यं कृशरान्नं च मुद्गान्नं यवपिष्टिकम् ॥
1.56.m: meat of various birds, turtle, porcupine, monitor lizard, hare, / oblation-food, kṛśarā, mung-bean rice, barley flour,

1.56.s:
matsyānnaṃ ca vicitrānnaṃ dadhyannaṃ dasrabhātkramāt /
bhuktvā rājebhāśvarathanarairyāti jayatyarīn //
1.56.d:
मत्स्यान्नं च विचित्रान्नं दध्यन्नं दस्रभात्क्रमात् ।
भुक्त्वा राजेभाश्वरथनरैर्याति जयत्यरीन् ॥
1.56.m: fish with rice, mixed rice, and curd-rice in order from the asterism Aśvinī— / having eaten these, the king marches with elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry and conquers his foes.

1.56.s:
hutāśanaṃ tilairhutvā pūjayeta digīśvaram /
praṇamya devabhūdevānāśīrvādairnṛpo vrajet //
1.56.d:
हुताशनं तिलैर्हुत्वा पूजयेत दिगीश्वरम् ।
प्रणम्य देवभूदेवानाशीर्वादैर्नृपो व्रजेत् ॥
1.56.m: Having offered sesame into the fire, he should worship the guardian of the directions; / having bowed to the gods and the Brahmins, the king should depart with blessings.

1.56.s:
yadvarṇavasragandhādyaistanmantreṇa vidhānataḥ /
indramairāvatārūḍhaṃ śacyā saha virājitam //
1.56.d:
यद्वर्णवस्रगन्धाद्यैस्तन्मन्त्रेण विधानतः ।
इन्द्रमैरावतारूढं शच्या सह विराजितम् ॥
1.56.m: Using clothes, perfumes, and other items of the appropriate color, and with the respective mantra according to the ritual rule: / Indra mounted on Airāvata, resplendent alongside Śacī,

1.56.s:
vajrapāṇiṃ svarṇavarṇaṃ divyābharaṇabhūṣitam /
saptahastaṃ saptajihvaṃ ṣaṇmukhaṃ meṣavāhanam //
1.56.d:
वज्रपाणिं स्वर्णवर्णं दिव्याभरणभूषितम् ।
सप्तहस्तं सप्तजिह्वं षण्मुखं मेषवाहनम् ॥
1.56.m: holding the thunderbolt, golden-hued, adorned with divine ornaments; / [Agni] seven-handed, seven-tongued, six-faced, riding a ram,

1.56.s:
svāhāpriye raktavarṇaṃ srukūsruvāyudhadhāriṇam /
daṇḍāyudhaṃ lohitārkṣaṃ yamaṃ mahiṣavāhanam //
1.56.d:
स्वाहाप्रिये रक्तवर्णं स्रुकूस्रुवायुधधारिणम् ।
दण्डायुधं लोहितार्क्षं यमं महिषवाहनम् ॥
1.56.m: the beloved of Svāhā, red-hued, bearing the sruc and sruva as weapons; / Yama holding the staff weapon, red-eyed, riding a buffalo,

1.56.s:
śyāmalaṃ sahitaṃ raktavarṇairūrddhvamukhaṃ śubham /
khaḍgacarmadharaṃ nīlaṃ nirṛtiṃ nakhāhanam //
1.56.d:
श्यामलं सहितं रक्तवर्णैरूर्द्ध्वमुखं शुभम् ।
खड्गचर्मधरं नीलं निरृतिं नखाहनम् ॥
1.56.m: dark-complexioned, accompanied by red hues, facing upwards, auspicious; / Nirṛti bearing a sword and shield, dark blue, riding an animal,

1.56.s:
urddhvakeśaṃ virūpākṣaṃ dīrghagrīvāyutaṃ vibhum /
nāgapāśadharaṃ pītavarṇaṃ makaravāhanam //
1.56.d:
उर्द्ध्वकेशं विरूपाक्षं दीर्घग्रीवायुतं विभुम् ।
नागपाशधरं पीतवर्णं मकरवाहनम् ॥
1.56.m: with hair standing upright, deformed eyes, endowed with a long neck, the all-pervading lord; / Varuṇa holding a serpent noose, yellow-colored, riding a makara,

1.56.s:
varuṇaṃ kālikānāthaṃ ratnābharaṇabhūṣitam /
prāṇināṃ prāṇarūpaṃ taṃ dvibāhuṃ daṇḍapāṇikam //
1.56.d:
वरुणं कालिकानाथं रत्नाभरणभूषितम् ।
प्राणिनां प्राणरूपं तं द्विबाहुं दण्डपाणिकम् ॥
1.56.m: the lord of Kālikā, adorned with gemstone ornaments; / Vāyu, the life-breath of living beings, two-armed, with staff in hand,

1.56.s:
vāyuṃ kṛṣṇamṛgārūḍhaṃ pūjayedañjanīpatim /
aśvārūḍhaṃ kuṃbhapāṇiṃ dvibāhuṃ svarṇasannibham //
1.56.d:
वायुं कृष्णमृगारूढं पूजयेदञ्जनीपतिम् ।
अश्वारूढं कुंभपाणिं द्विबाहुं स्वर्णसन्निभम् ॥
1.56.m: riding a black deer, the lord of Añjanī, him he should worship; / Kubera riding a horse, holding a jar, two-armed, resembling gold,

1.56.s:
kuberaṃ citralekheśaṃ yakṣagandharvanāyakam /
pinākinaṃ vṛṣārūḍhaṃ gaurīpatimanuttam //
1.56.d:
कुबेरं चित्रलेखेशं यक्षगन्धर्वनायकम् ।
पिनाकिनं वृषारूढं गौरीपतिमनुत्तम् ॥
1.56.m: the lord of Citralekhā, leader of the Yakṣas and Gandharvas; / Pinākin riding a bull, the matchless lord of Gaurī,

1.56.s:
śvetavarṇaṃ candramauliṃ nāgayajñopavītinam /
aprayāṇe svayaṃ kāryā prekṣayā bhūbhujastathā //
1.56.d:
श्वेतवर्णं चन्द्रमौलिं नागयज्ञोपवीतिनम् ।
अप्रयाणे स्वयं कार्या प्रेक्षया भूभुजस्तथा ॥
1.56.m: white-hued, with the moon on his crest, wearing a snake as his sacred thread. / If the king cannot march in person, it should be done by proxy through inspection;

1.56.s:
kāryaṃ nigamanaṃ chatraṃ dhvajaśastrāstravāhanaiḥ /
svasthānānnirgamasthānaṃ daḍānāṃ ca śatandvayam //
1.56.d:
कार्यं निगमनं छत्रं ध्वजशस्त्रास्त्रवाहनैः ।
स्वस्थानान्निर्गमस्थानं दडानां च शतन्द्वयम् ॥
1.56.m: the dispatch should be carried out using the umbrella, standard, weapons, missiles, and mounts. / The place of departure from one's own dwelling should be two hundred daṇḍas,

1.56.s:
catvāriṃśaddvādaśaiva prasthitaḥ sa svayaṃ gataḥ /
dinānyekatra na vasetsaptaṣṭ vā paro janaḥ //
1.56.d:
चत्वारिंशद्द्वादशैव प्रस्थितः स स्वयं गतः ।
दिनान्येकत्र न वसेत्सप्तष्ट् वा परो जनः ॥
1.56.m: or forty, or even twelve [daṇḍas]; then he who has set out is deemed to have gone in person. / Another person should not dwell in one single place for seven or eight days;

1.56.s:
pañcarātraṃ ca purataḥ punarlagnāntare vrajet /
akālajeṣu nṛpatirvidyudgarjitavṛṣṭiṣu //
1.56.d:
पञ्चरात्रं च पुरतः पुनर्लग्नान्तरे व्रजेत् ।
अकालजेषु नृपतिर्विद्युद्गर्जितवृष्टिषु ॥
1.56.m: furthermore, after five nights ahead, he may march again in another auspicious lagna. / In the event of unseasonal lightning, thunder, and rain,

1.56.s:
utpāteṣu trividheṣu saptarātraṃ tu na vrajet /
sntākuḍyaśivākākakapotānāṃ girastathā //
1.56.d:
उत्पातेषु त्रिविधेषु सप्तरात्रं तु न व्रजेत् ।
स्न्ताकुड्यशिवाकाककपोतानां गिरस्तथा ॥
1.56.m: or the three kinds of portents, he should not march for seven nights. / The cries of the snake-catching bird, a lizard, a jackal, a crow, and a pigeon,

1.56.s:
jhajhebhukhemavakṣīrasvarāṇāṃ vāmato gatiḥ /
pītakārabharadvājapabhiṇāṃ dakṣiṇā gatiḥ //
1.56.d:
झझेभुखेमवक्षीरस्वराणां वामतो गतिः ।
पीतकारभरद्वाजपभिणां दक्षिणा गतिः ॥
1.56.m: as well as the calls of the cricket, owl, mongoose, and dog are auspicious when passing to the left; / the movement of the woodpecker and the skylark is auspicious on the right.

1.56.s:
cāṣaṃ tyaktvā catuṣpāttu śubhadāvāmato matāḥ /
kṛṣṇaṃ tyaktvā prayāṇe tu kṛkalāsena vīkṣitaḥ //
1.56.d:
चाषं त्यक्त्वा चतुष्पात्तु शुभदावामतो मताः ।
कृष्णं त्यक्त्वा प्रयाणे तु कृकलासेन वीक्षितः ॥
1.56.m: Except for the blue jay, four-footed animals are considered auspicious on the left. / At departure, being seen by a chameleon, except for a black one,

1.56.s:
vārāhaśaśagodhāstu sarpāṇāṃ kīrtanaṃ śubham /
hṛtekṣaṇaṃ neṣṭamevāvyapatyayaṃ kapiṛkṣayoḥ //
1.56.d:
वाराहशशगोधास्तु सर्पाणां कीर्तनं शुभम् ।
हृतेक्षणं नेष्टमेवाव्यपत्ययं कपिऋक्षयोः ॥
1.56.m: or the mere mention of a boar, hare, monitor lizard, and snakes is auspicious; / having one's sight obstructed is not desirable, nor is the sudden crossing of a monkey or a bear.

1.56.s:
mayūracchāganakulacāṣapārāvatāḥ śubhāḥ /
dṛṣṭamātreṇa yātrāyāṃ vyastaṃ sarvaṃ praveśane //
1.56.d:
मयूरच्छागनकुलचाषपारावताः शुभाः ।
दृष्टमात्रेण यात्रायां व्यस्तं सर्वं प्रवेशने ॥
1.56.m: Peacocks, goats, mongooses, blue jays, and pigeons are auspicious / at the mere sight during departure; the opposite is true upon entry.

1.56.s:
yātrāsiddhirbhaveddṛṣṭe śaverādanavajite /
praveśe rodanayutaḥ śavaḥ śavapradastathā //
1.56.d:
यात्रासिद्धिर्भवेद्दृष्टे शवेरादनवजिते ।
प्रवेशे रोदनयुतः शवः शवप्रदस्तथा ॥
1.56.m: Success in an expedition occurs upon seeing a corpse devoid of weeping; / upon entry, a corpse accompanied by weeping causes death.

1.56.s:
patitaklībajaṭilamattavāntauṣadhādibhiḥ /
abhyaktavasāsthicarmāṅgāradāruṇarogibhiḥ //
1.56.d:
पतितक्लीबजटिलमत्तवान्तौषधादिभिः ।
अभ्यक्तवसास्थिचर्माङ्गारदारुणरोगिभिः ॥
1.56.m: A fallen man, an impotent man, one with matted hair, an intoxicated person, vomited medicine and the like, / persons anointed with fat, bones, hides, burning coals, or severe diseases,

1.56.s:
guḍakārpāsalavaṇaripupraśnatṛṇoragaiḥ /
vandhyākuñjakakāṣāyamuktakeśabubhukṣitaiḥ //
1.56.d:
गुडकार्पासलवणरिपुप्रश्नतृणोरगैः ।
वन्ध्याकुञ्जककाषायमुक्तकेशबुभुक्षितैः ॥
1.56.m: jaggery, cotton, salt, an enemy, one asking questions, grass, serpents, / a barren woman, an eunuch, one wearing saffron robes, disheveled hair, starving persons,

1.56.s:
prayāṇasamaye nagnairddṛṣṭaiḥ siddhirna jāyate /
prajvalāgnīnsuturaganṛpāsanapurāṅganāḥ //
1.56.d:
प्रयाणसमये नग्नैर्द्दृष्टैः सिद्धिर्न जायते ।
प्रज्वलाग्नीन्सुतुरगनृपासनपुराङ्गनाः ॥
1.56.m: and naked persons seen at the time of departure bring no success. / Blazing fires, fine horses, the royal throne, city women,

1.56.s:
gandhapuṣaapākṣatacchatracāmarāndolikaṃ nṛpaḥ /
bhakṣyekṣuphalamṛtsnānnamadhvājyadadhigodayāḥ //
1.56.d:
गन्धपुषअपाक्षतच्छत्रचामरान्दोलिकं नृपः ।
भक्ष्येक्षुफलमृत्स्नान्नमध्वाज्यदधिगोदयाः ॥
1.56.m: Fragrance, flowers, unhusked rice, an umbrella, a cāmara, a litter, a king, / sweetmeats, sugarcane, fruit, fine clay, food, honey, ghee, curd, the rising of cattle,

1.56.s:
madyamāṃsasudhādhautavastraśaṅkhavṛṣadhvajāḥ /
puṇyastrīpuṇyakalaśaratnabhṛṅgāragodvijāḥ //
1.56.d:
मद्यमांससुधाधौतवस्त्रशङ्खवृषध्वजाः ।
पुण्यस्त्रीपुण्यकलशरत्नभृङ्गारगोद्विजाः ॥
1.56.m: liquor, meat, nectar, washed cloth, a conch, an ox, banners, / an auspicious woman, a sacred water-pot, a jewel, a pitcher, cattle, twice-born men,

1.56.s:
bherīmṛdaṅgapaṭahaghaṇṭāvīṇādiniḥsvanāḥ /
vedamaṅgalaghoṣāḥ syuḥ yā yināṃ kāryasiddhidāḥ //
1.56.d:
भेरीमृदङ्गपटहघण्टावीणादिनिःस्वनाः ।
वेदमङ्गलघोषाः स्युः या यिनां कार्यसिद्धिदाः ॥
1.56.m: the sounds of kettledrums, mṛdaṅgas, paṭahas, bells, vīṇās, and the like, / [and] the auspicious chanting of the Vedas—these grant success in undertakings to travelers.

1.56.s:
ādau viruddhaśakunaṃ dṛṣṭvā yāyīṣṭadevatām /
smṛtvā dvitīye viprāṇāṃ kṛtvā pūjāṃ nivartayet //
1.56.d:
आदौ विरुद्धशकुनं दृष्ट्वा यायीष्टदेवताम् ।
स्मृत्वा द्वितीये विप्राणां कृत्वा पूजां निवर्तयेत् ॥
1.56.m: Seeing an unfavourable omen at the outset, a traveler should remember his chosen deity; / on a second [such omen], he should make an offering to the Brahmins and turn back.

1.56.s:
sarvadikṣukṣutaṃ neṣṭaṃ gokṣutaṃ nidhanapradam /
aphalaṃ yadbālavṛddharogipainasikaiḥ kṛtam //
1.56.d:
सर्वदिक्षुक्षुतं नेष्टं गोक्षुतं निधनप्रदम् ।
अफलं यद्बालवृद्धरोगिपैनसिकैः कृतम् ॥
1.56.m: Sneezing in all directions is undesirable, and the sneeze of a cow brings death; / [a sneeze] made by children, the aged, the diseased, or those with catarrh is without effect.

1.56.s:
parastrī dvijadevasvaṃ tatrapṛśeddiggajāśvakān /
hanyātparapuraprāpto na strīrnityaṃ nirāyudhān //
1.56.d:
परस्त्री द्विजदेवस्वं तत्रपृशेद्दिग्गजाश्वकान् ।
हन्यात्परपुरप्राप्तो न स्त्रीर्नित्यं निरायुधान् ॥
1.56.m: Another’s wife, the property of twice-born men and gods, and the quarter-elephants and horses there he must not touch; / having reached an enemy city, he must never slay women or those without weapons.

1.56.s:
ādau saumyāyane kāryaṃnavavāstupraveśanam /
vidhāya pūrvadivase vāstupūjābalikriyām //
1.56.d:
आदौ सौम्यायने कार्यंनववास्तुप्रवेशनम् ।
विधाय पूर्वदिवसे वास्तुपूजाबलिक्रियाम् ॥
1.56.m: The entry into a new house should first be performed in the northern course of the sun, / having performed the worship of the site and the offering of oblations on the preceding day.

1.56.s:
māghaphaālgunavaiśākhajyeṣṭamāseṣu śobhanam /
praveśo madhyamo jñeyaḥ saumyakārtikamāsayoḥ //
1.56.d:
माघफआल्गुनवैशाखज्येष्टमासेषु शोभनम् ।
प्रवेशो मध्यमो ज्ञेयः सौम्यकार्तिकमासयोः ॥
1.56.m: In the months of Māgha, Phālguna, Vaiśākha, and Jyeṣṭha it is auspicious; / house-entry should be known as middling in the months of Mārgaśīrṣa and Kārttika.

1.56.s:
śaśījyānteṣu varuṇatvāṣṭramitrasthiroḍuṣu /
śubhaḥ prevaśo devejyaśukrayorddṛśyamānayoḥ //
1.56.d:
शशीज्यान्तेषु वरुणत्वाष्ट्रमित्रस्थिरोडुषु ।
शुभः प्रेवशो देवेज्यशुक्रयोर्द्दृश्यमानयोः ॥
1.56.m: In the lunar mansions ending with Jupiter's and the Moon's, in Śatabhiṣaj, Citrā, Anurādhā, and the fixed stars, / house-entry is auspicious while Jupiter and Venus are visible,

1.56.s:
vyarkāravāre tithiṣu riktāmāvarjiteṣu ca /
divā vā yadi vā rātrau praveśo maṅgalapradaḥ //
1.56.d:
व्यर्कारवारे तिथिषु रिक्तामावर्जितेषु च ।
दिवा वा यदि वा रात्रौ प्रवेशो मङ्गलप्रदः ॥
1.56.m: on weekdays other than Sunday, and on lunar days avoiding the empty ones and the new moon; / whether by day or by night, the entry brings auspiciousness,

1.56.s:
candratārābalopete pūrvāhne śobhane dine /
sthiralagne sthirāṃśe ca naidhane śuddhisaṃyute //
1.56.d:
चन्द्रताराबलोपेते पूर्वाह्ने शोभने दिने ।
स्थिरलग्ने स्थिरांशे च नैधने शुद्धिसंयुते ॥
1.56.m: endowed with the strength of the Moon and lunar mansions, in the forenoon of an auspicious day, / in a fixed ascendant and fixed degree, and with purity in the eighth house,

1.56.s:
trikoṇakendrasaṃsthaiś saumyaistryāyārigaiḥ paraiḥ /
lagrāntyāṣṭamaṣaṣṭasthavarjitena dviyāṃśunā //
1.56.d:
त्रिकोणकेन्द्रसंस्थैश् सौम्यैस्त्र्यायारिगैः परैः ।
लग्रान्त्याष्टमषष्टस्थवर्जितेन द्वियांशुना ॥
1.56.m: with benefics situated in trines and angles, and others in the third, eleventh, and sixth [houses], / avoiding the Sun situated in the ascendant, twelfth, eighth, or sixth [houses].

1.56.s:
karturṣā janmabhe lagne tābhyāmupacaye 'pi vā /
praveśalgne syāmṛddhiranyabheśokaniḥsvatā //
1.56.d:
कर्तुर्षा जन्मभे लग्ने ताभ्यामुपचये ऽपि वा ।
प्रवेशल्ग्ने स्यामृद्धिरन्यभेशोकनिःस्वता ॥
1.56.m: In the builder's asterism, birth-asterism, ascendant, or in an upacaya from both of them, / in the ascendant of entry there will be prosperity; in any other asterism, sorrow and poverty.

1.56.s:
darśanīya gṛhaṃ ramyaṃ vidhidhairmaṅgalasvanaiḥ /
kṛtvārkaṃ vāmato vidvānbhṛṅgāraṃ cāgrato viśet //
1.56.d:
दर्शनीय गृहं रम्यं विधिधैर्मङ्गलस्वनैः ।
कृत्वार्कं वामतो विद्वान्भृङ्गारं चाग्रतो विशेत् ॥
1.56.m: Looking upon the charming house with various auspicious sounds, / having kept the Sun on his left, the wise man should enter with a water-pot in front.

1.56.s:
varṣāpraveśe śaśini jalarāśigatepi vā /
kendrage vā śuklapakṣe cātivṛṣṭiḥ śubhekṣite //
1.56.d:
वर्षाप्रवेशे शशिनि जलराशिगतेपि वा ।
केन्द्रगे वा शुक्लपक्षे चातिवृष्टिः शुभेक्षिते ॥
1.56.m: At the onset of the rainy season, when the Moon is in a watery sign / or in an angle during the bright fortnight, and aspected by a benefic, there is excessive rain;

1.56.s:
alpavṛṣṭiḥ pāpadṛṣṭe prāvṛṭkāle 'cirādbhavet /
candraśceddhārgave sarvamevaṃvidha guṇānvite //
1.56.d:
अल्पवृष्टिः पापदृष्टे प्रावृट्काले ऽचिराद्भवेत् ।
चन्द्रश्चेद्धार्गवे सर्वमेवंविध गुणान्विते ॥
1.56.m: if aspected by a malefic, there will soon be meager rain in the rainy season. / If the Moon is with Venus, all endowed with such qualities,

1.56.s:
prāvṛṣīnduḥ sitātsaptarāśigaḥ śubhavīkṣitaḥ /
mandātrrikoṇasaptastho yadi vā vṛddhikṛdbhavet //
1.56.d:
प्रावृषीन्दुः सितात्सप्तराशिगः शुभवीक्षितः ।
मन्दात्र्रिकोणसप्तस्थो यदि वा वृद्धिकृद्भवेत् ॥
1.56.m: the Moon in the rainy season occupying the seventh sign from Venus, aspected by a benefic, / or situated in a trine or the seventh from Saturn, causes an increase [of rain].

1.56.s:
sadyo vṛṣṭikaraḥ śukro yadā budhasamīpagaḥ /
tayorṃmadhyagate bhānau bhavedṣṭivināśanam //
1.56.d:
सद्यो वृष्टिकरः शुक्रो यदा बुधसमीपगः ।
तयोर्ंमध्यगते भानौ भवेद्ष्टिविनाशनम् ॥
1.56.m: Venus produces immediate rain when it goes near Mercury; / when the Sun enters between the two, there will be destruction of rain.

1.56.s:
maghādipañcadhiṣṇyasthaḥ pūrve svātitraye pare /
pravarṣaṇaṃ bhṛguḥ kuryādviparīte na varṣaṇam //
1.56.d:
मघादिपञ्चधिष्ण्यस्थः पूर्वे स्वातित्रये परे ।
प्रवर्षणं भृगुः कुर्याद्विपरीते न वर्षणम् ॥
1.56.m: Situated in the five mansions beginning with Maghā in the east, or the three beginning with Svātī in the west, / Venus produces rainfall; in the reverse, there is no rain.

1.56.s:
purataḥ pṛṣṭato bhānorgrahā yadi samīpagāḥ /
tadā vṛṣṭiṃ prakurvanti na te cetpratilomagāḥ //
1.56.d:
पुरतः पृष्टतो भानोर्ग्रहा यदि समीपगाः ।
तदा वृष्टिं प्रकुर्वन्ति न ते चेत्प्रतिलोमगाः ॥
1.56.m: If planets are situated close before or behind the Sun, / they produce rain then, provided they are not moving retrogradely.

1.56.s:
vāmabhāgasthitaḥ śukro vṛṣṭikṛccettu yāmyagaḥ /
udayāsteṣu vṛṣṭiḥ syādbhānorārdrāpraveśane //
1.56.d:
वामभागस्थितः शुक्रो वृष्टिकृच्चेत्तु याम्यगः ।
उदयास्तेषु वृष्टिः स्याद्भानोरार्द्राप्रवेशने ॥
1.56.m: If Venus situated on the left side brings rain, then if it goes to the south, / there will be rain at its rising and setting, [and] at the Sun's entry into Ārdrā.

1.56.s:
saṃdhyayoḥ sasyavṛddhiḥ syātsarvasaṃpannṛṇānniśi /
stokavṛṣṭiranarghaḥ syādavṛṣṭiḥ sasyasaṃpadaḥ //
1.56.d:
संध्ययोः सस्यवृद्धिः स्यात्सर्वसंपन्नृणान्निशि ।
स्तोकवृष्टिरनर्घः स्यादवृष्टिः सस्यसंपदः ॥
1.56.m: At the two twilights there will be growth of crops; at night, complete prosperity for men; / with little rain there will be high prices; with no rain, prosperity of crops [is ruined].

1.56.s:
ādrodayegrabhinnā cadbhavediti na saṃśayaḥ /
candrejye jñetha vā śukre kendrenbītirvinaśyati //
1.56.d:
आद्रोदयेग्रभिन्ना चद्भवेदिति न संशयः ।
चन्द्रेज्ये ज्ञेथ वा शुक्रे केन्द्रेन्बीतिर्विनश्यति ॥
1.56.m: If clouds are broken at the rising of Ārdrā, there is no doubt [of this]; / if the Moon, Jupiter, Mercury, or Venus is in an angle, calamity is destroyed.

1.56.s:
pūrvāṣāḍhā gato bhānurjīmūtaiḥ pariveṣṭitaḥ /
varṣatyārdrādimṛlāntaṃ pratyakṣaṃ pratyahaṃ tathā //
1.56.d:
पूर्वाषाढा गतो भानुर्जीमूतैः परिवेष्टितः ।
वर्षत्यार्द्रादिमृलान्तं प्रत्यक्षं प्रत्यहं तथा ॥
1.56.m: The Sun situated in Pūrvāṣāḍhā, surrounded by clouds, / rains daily and visibly from Ārdrā to Mūla.

1.56.s:
vṛṣṭiścetpauṣṇabheṃ tasmāddaśarkṣeṣu na varṣati /
siṃhe bhinne kujo vṛṣṭirabhinne karkaṭe tathā //
1.56.d:
वृष्टिश्चेत्पौष्णभें तस्माद्दशर्क्षेषु न वर्षति ।
सिंहे भिन्ने कुजो वृष्टिरभिन्ने कर्कटे तथा ॥
1.56.m: If it rains in Revatī, it does not rain for ten asterisms from that; / when Leo is pierced, Mars brings rain; likewise when Cancer is not pierced.

1.56.s:
kanyodaye prabhinne cetsarvadā vṛṣṭiruttama /
ahirbudhnyaṃ pūrvaśasyaṃ paraśasyā ca revatī //
1.56.d:
कन्योदये प्रभिन्ने चेत्सर्वदा वृष्टिरुत्तम ।
अहिर्बुध्न्यं पूर्वशस्यं परशस्या च रेवती ॥
1.56.m: If it is pierced at the rising of Virgo, there is always excellent rain; / Uttarabhadrapadā brings early crops, and Revatī brings late crops;

1.56.s:
bharaṇī sarvasasyā ca sarvanāśāya cāśvinī /
guroḥ saptamarā tisthaḥ pratyaggo bhṛgujo yadā //
1.56.d:
भरणी सर्वसस्या च सर्वनाशाय चाश्विनी ।
गुरोः सप्तमरा तिस्थः प्रत्यग्गो भृगुजो यदा ॥
1.56.m: Bharaṇī brings all crops, and Aśvinī brings complete destruction. / When Venus, moving westward, is situated in the seventh sign from Jupiter,

1.56.s:
tadātivarṣaṇaṃ bhūri prāvṛṭkāle balojjhite /
āsaptamarkṣaṃśaśinaḥ pariveśagatottarā //
1.56.d:
तदातिवर्षणं भूरि प्रावृट्काले बलोज्झिते ।
आसप्तमर्क्षंशशिनः परिवेशगतोत्तरा ॥
1.56.m: then there is abundant, heavy rainfall during the rainy season, even if depleted of strength. / If a halo of the Moon extends up to the seventh asterism to the north,

1.56.s:
vidyutprapūrṇamaṇḍūkāsvanāvṛṣṭirbhavettadā /
yadāpratyaṅnatā maghāḥ khasaptopari saṃsthitāḥ //
1.56.d:
विद्युत्प्रपूर्णमण्डूकास्वनावृष्टिर्भवेत्तदा ।
यदाप्रत्यङ्नता मघाः खसप्तोपरि संस्थिताः ॥
1.56.m: with lightning and filled with the croaking of frogs, then rain occurs. / When Maghā stars bending westward are situated high above seven in the sky,

1.56.s:
patanti dakṣiṇasthā yebhavedvṛṣṭistadācirāt /
nakhairlikhantomārjārāścāvaniṃ lohasaṃyute //
1.56.d:
पतन्ति दक्षिणस्था येभवेद्वृष्टिस्तदाचिरात् ।
नखैर्लिखन्तोमार्जाराश्चावनिं लोहसंयुते ॥
1.56.m: and fall while situated in the south, rain will occur soon after. / Cats scratching the earth with their claws, [or] in contact with iron,

1.56.s:
rathyāyāṃ setubandhāḥ syurbālānāṃ vṛṣṭihetavaḥ /
pipīlikāśreṇayaśchinnāḥ khadyotā bahavastadā //
1.56.d:
रथ्यायां सेतुबन्धाः स्युर्बालानां वृष्टिहेतवः ।
पिपीलिकाश्रेणयश्छिन्नाः खद्योता बहवस्तदा ॥
1.56.m: children building bridges in the street—these are causes of rain. / Broken lines of ants and many fireflies then,

1.56.s:
drumādirohaḥ sarpāṇāṃ prītirdurvṛṣṭisūcakāḥ /
udayāstamaye kāle vivarṇor'ketha vā śaśī //
1.56.d:
द्रुमादिरोहः सर्पाणां प्रीतिर्दुर्वृष्टिसूचकाः ।
उदयास्तमये काले विवर्णोर्ऽकेथ वा शशी ॥
1.56.m: snakes climbing trees and the like, and their coupling, indicate bad rain. / If at sunrise or sunset the Sun or Moon is discolored

1.56.s:
madhuvarṇo 'tivāyuścedativṛṣṭirbhavettadā /
prāṅmukhasya tu kūrmasya navāṅgeṣu dharāmimām //
1.56.d:
मधुवर्णो ऽतिवायुश्चेदतिवृष्टिर्भवेत्तदा ।
प्राङ्मुखस्य तु कूर्मस्य नवाङ्गेषु धरामिमाम् ॥
1.56.m: or honey-colored, and if there is excessive wind, then there will be heavy rain. / Dividing this earth into nine parts upon the nine limbs of the tortoise facing east,

1.56.s:
vibhajya navadhā khaṇḍe maṇḍalāni pradakṣiṇam /
antarvedāśca ṣāñcālastasyedaṃ nābhimaṇḍalam //
1.56.d:
विभज्य नवधा खण्डे मण्डलानि प्रदक्षिणम् ।
अन्तर्वेदाश्च षाञ्चालस्तस्येदं नाभिमण्डलम् ॥
1.56.m: the regions in clockwise order: Antarvedi and the Pāñcālas are its navel region;

1.56.s:
prācyā māgadhalāṭotthā deśāstanmukhamaṇḍalam /
strīkaliṅgakirātākhyā deśāstadbāhumaṇḍalam //
1.56.d:
प्राच्या मागधलाटोत्था देशास्तन्मुखमण्डलम् ।
स्त्रीकलिङ्गकिराताख्या देशास्तद्बाहुमण्डलम् ॥
1.56.m: the eastern countries, and those arising in Magadha and Lāṭa, are its face region; / the regions called Strīrājya, Kaliṅga, and Kirāta are its right arm region;

1.56.s:
avantī draviḍā bhillā deśāstatpārśvamaṇḍalam /
gauḍakaiṅkaṇaśālvāndhrapauḍrastatpādamaṇḍalam //
1.56.d:
अवन्ती द्रविडा भिल्ला देशास्तत्पार्श्वमण्डलम् ।
गौडकैङ्कणशाल्वान्ध्रपौड्रस्तत्पादमण्डलम् ॥
1.56.m: Avanti, the Draviḍas, and the Bhillas are its right side region; / Gauḍa, Koṅkaṇa, Śālva, Andhra, and Pauṇḍra are its right foot region;

1.56.s:
siṃdhukāśimahārāṣṭrasaurāṣṭrāḥ pucchamaṇḍalam /
pulindacīnayavanagurjarāḥ pādamaṇḍalam //
1.56.d:
सिंधुकाशिमहाराष्ट्रसौराष्ट्राः पुच्छमण्डलम् ।
पुलिन्दचीनयवनगुर्जराः पादमण्डलम् ॥
1.56.m: Sindhu, Kāśi, Mahārāṣṭra, and Saurāṣṭra are the tail region; / the Pulindas, Cīnas, Yavanas, and Gurjaras are the left foot region;

1.56.s:
kurukāśmīramādreyamatsyāstatpārśvamaṇḍalam /
khasāṃgavaṅgabāhlīkaṃ kāṃbojāḥ pāṇimaṇḍalam //
1.56.d:
कुरुकाश्मीरमाद्रेयमत्स्यास्तत्पार्श्वमण्डलम् ।
खसांगवङ्गबाह्लीकं कांबोजाः पाणिमण्डलम् ॥
1.56.m: Kuru, Kaśmīra, Mādreya, and Matsya are its left side region; / Khasa, Aṅga, Vaṅga, Bāhlīka, and the Kāmbojas are its left arm region.

1.56.s:
kṛttikādīni dhiṣṇyāni trīṇi triṇi kramānnyaset /
nābhyādiṣu navāṅgeṣu pāpairduṣṭaṃ śubhaiḥ śubham //
1.56.d:
कृत्तिकादीनि धिष्ण्यानि त्रीणि त्रिणि क्रमान्न्यसेत् ।
नाभ्यादिषु नवाङ्गेषु पापैर्दुष्टं शुभैः शुभम् ॥
1.56.m: One should assign the lunar mansions beginning with Kṛttikā in groups of three successively / to the nine limbs beginning with the navel; affliction comes from malefics, and good from benefics.

1.56.s:
devatā yatra nṛtyanti patanti prajvalanti ca /
muhū rudanti gāyanti prasvidyanti hasaṃti ca //
1.56.d:
देवता यत्र नृत्यन्ति पतन्ति प्रज्वलन्ति च ।
मुहू रुदन्ति गायन्ति प्रस्विद्यन्ति हसंति च ॥
1.56.m: Where deities dance, fall, flare up, / repeatedly weep, sing, sweat, and laugh,

1.56.s:
vamantyagniṃ tathā dhūmaṃ snehaṃ raktaṃ payo jalam /
adhomukhādhitiṣṭanti sthānātsthānaṃ vrajanti ca //
1.56.d:
वमन्त्यग्निं तथा धूमं स्नेहं रक्तं पयो जलम् ।
अधोमुखाधितिष्टन्ति स्थानात्स्थानं व्रजन्ति च ॥
1.56.m: vomit fire, smoke, oil, blood, milk, or water, / hang upside down, and move from place to place—

1.56.s:
evamādyā hi dṛśyante vikārāḥ pratimāsu ca /
gandharvanagaraṃ caiva divā nakṣatradarśanam //
1.56.d:
एवमाद्या हि दृश्यन्ते विकाराः प्रतिमासु च ।
गन्धर्वनगरं चैव दिवा नक्षत्रदर्शनम् ॥
1.56.m: when such portents are seen in idols, and a city of the Gandharvas, or the sight of stars by day,

1.56.s:
mahotkāpatanaṃ kāṣṭatṛṇaraktapravarṣaṇam /
gāndharvaṃ dehadigdhūmaṃ bhūmikaṃpaṃ divā niśi //
1.56.d:
महोत्कापतनं काष्टतृणरक्तप्रवर्षणम् ।
गान्धर्वं देहदिग्धूमं भूमिकंपं दिवा निशि ॥
1.56.m: the falling of great meteors, a rain of wood, grass, and blood, / celestial sounds, smoke rising from bodies or the quarters, earthquakes by day and night,

1.56.s:
anagnau ca sphuliṅgāśca jvalanaṃ ca vinendhanam /
niśīndracāpamaṇḍūkaṃ śikhare śvetavāyasaḥ //
1.56.d:
अनग्नौ च स्फुलिङ्गाश्च ज्वलनं च विनेन्धनम् ।
निशीन्द्रचापमण्डूकं शिखरे श्वेतवायसः ॥
1.56.m: sparks where there is no fire, and burning without fuel, / a rainbow at night, a frog or a white crow on a roof-peak,

1.56.s:
dṛśyante visphuliṅgāśca gogajāśvoṣṭragātrataḥ /
jantavo dvitriśiraso jāyante vāpi yoniṣu //
1.56.d:
दृश्यन्ते विस्फुलिङ्गाश्च गोगजाश्वोष्ट्रगात्रतः ।
जन्तवो द्वित्रिशिरसो जायन्ते वापि योनिषु ॥
1.56.m: sparks seen from the limbs of cows, elephants, horses, and camels, / or creatures born from wombs with two or three heads,

1.56.s:
prātaḥ sūryāścatasṛṣu hyarditāyugapadraveḥ /
jambūkagrāmasaṃvāsaḥ ketūnāṃ ca pradarśanam //
1.56.d:
प्रातः सूर्याश्चतसृषु ह्यर्दितायुगपद्रवेः ।
जम्बूकग्रामसंवासः केतूनां च प्रदर्शनम् ॥
1.56.m: the Sun seen in the four directions in the morning afflicted simultaneously, / jackals dwelling in villages, and the appearance of comets,

1.56.s:
kākānāmākulaṃ rātrau kapotānāṃ divā yadi /
akāle puṣpitā vṛkṣā dṛśyante phalitā yadi //
1.56.d:
काकानामाकुलं रात्रौ कपोतानां दिवा यदि ।
अकाले पुष्पिता वृक्षा दृश्यन्ते फलिता यदि ॥
1.56.m: commotion among crows at night, or among pigeons by day, / if trees are seen flowering or bearing fruit out of season—

1.56.s:
kāryaṃ tacchedanaṃ tatra tataḥ śāntirmanīṣibhiḥ /
evamādyā mahotpātā bahavaḥ sthānanāśadā //
1.56.d:
कार्यं तच्छेदनं तत्र ततः शान्तिर्मनीषिभिः ।
एवमाद्या महोत्पाता बहवः स्थाननाशदा ॥
1.56.m: they must be cut down there, and then an appeasement ritual performed by the wise; / such great portents, many in number, cause the destruction of the place.

1.56.s:
kecinmṛtyupradāḥ kecicchatrubhyaśca bhayapradāḥ /
madhyādbhayaṃ yaśo mṛtyuḥ kṣayaḥ kīrtiḥ sukhāsukham //
1.56.d:
केचिन्मृत्युप्रदाः केचिच्छत्रुभ्यश्च भयप्रदाः ।
मध्याद्भयं यशो मृत्युः क्षयः कीर्तिः सुखासुखम् ॥
1.56.m: Some bring death, and some bring fear from enemies; / fear from the middle, renown, death, decay, fame, pleasure and pain,

1.56.s:
aisvaryaṃ dhanahāniṃ ca madhucchannaṃ ca vālmikam /
ityādiṣu ca sarveṣūtpāteṣu dvijasattama //
1.56.d:
ऐस्वर्यं धनहानिं च मधुच्छन्नं च वाल्मिकम् ।
इत्यादिषु च सर्वेषूत्पातेषु द्विजसत्तम ॥
1.56.m: lordship, loss of wealth, [a sign of] dripping honey, or an anthill. / Amid these and all other portents, O best of the twice-born,

1.56.s:
śāntiṃ kuryātprayatnena kalpoktavidhinā śubham /
ityetatkathitaṃ vipra jyautiṣaṃ te samāsataḥ //
1.56.d:
शान्तिं कुर्यात्प्रयत्नेन कल्पोक्तविधिना शुभम् ।
इत्येतत्कथितं विप्र ज्यौतिषं ते समासतः ॥
1.56.m: one should diligently perform an auspicious propitiatory rite according to the prescribed rules. / Thus, O brāhmaṇa, astrology has been told to you in brief.

1.56.s:
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi cchandaḥ śāstramanuttamam //
iti śrībṛhanna.pūrva.bṛhadupākhyāne dvitīyapāde ṣaṭpañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.56.d:
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि च्छन्दः शास्त्रमनुत्तमम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्न।पूर्व।बृहदुपाख्याने द्वितीयपादे षट्पञ्चाशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
1.56.m:
Hereafter I shall proclaim the unsurpassed science of metrics.

Thus ends the fifty-sixth chapter in the second quarter of the Bṛhadupākhyāna in the glorious Bṛhannāradīya.
